When you put an object into a fluid, the object pushes aside (displaces) an amount of fluid equal to the space it occupies. Archimedes discovered that the upward buoyant force on the object equals exactly the weight of this displaced fluid.
잠긴 부피 V_잠김에 해당하는 유체 무게가 부력이므로 F_b = ρ_유체: Since the buoyant force is the weight of fluid corresponding to the submerged volume V_submerged, F_b = ρ_fluid · g · V_submerged. Meanwhile, the object's weight is W = ρ_object · g · V_object.
When an object floats in equilibrium at the surface, the buoyant force equals the weight (F_b = W). Setting the two expressions equal, the submerged-volume fraction equals the ratio of the two densities: V_submerged / V_object = ρ_object / ρ_fluid. If this ratio is less than 1 (ρ_object < ρ_fluid), the object floats partly submerged; if it is 1 or more (ρ_object ≥ ρ_fluid), it becomes fully submerged and sinks.
흔한 오개념 — \"무거운 물체는 가라앉고 가벼운 물체는 뜬다\"고 흔히: Common misconception — people often think "heavy objects sink and light objects float." But a huge steel ship weighs thousands of tons, extremely heavy, yet floats on water. What determines floating or sinking is not total weight but average density. A ship floats because it is hollow inside, so its average density is less than that of water.

The larger the eccentricity e, the greater the speed difference between perihelion and aphelion. Increasing the semi-major axis a makes the orbit larger and the orbital period T longer (T² ∝ a³).

태양-행성 선분이 같은 시간에 같은 면적을 쓸어냄(면적속도 일정)을 이해: Understand that the Sun–planet line sweeps out equal areas in equal times (constant areal velocity) (2nd law).
Explain, from constant areal velocity, why a planet is fast at perihelion and slow at aphelion.
Learn the relationship between orbital period and semi-major axis, T² ∝ a³ (3rd law).
Grasp how the eccentricity e determines the flatness of the orbit and the variation in speed.
1법칙 (타원 궤도): 모든 행성은 태양을 두 초점 중 하나로 하는 타원: 1st law (elliptical orbit): Every planet moves in an elliptical orbit with the Sun at one of the two foci. When the eccentricity e is 0 it is a perfect circle, and as e increases the ellipse becomes flatter. Letting the semi-major axis be a and the eccentricity be e, the perihelion distance nearest the Sun (focus) is a(1−e), and the aphelion distance farthest away is a(1+e).
2법칙 (면적속도 일정): 태양과 행성을 잇는 선분은 같은 시간 동안 항: 2nd law (constant areal velocity): The line joining the Sun and a planet always sweeps out equal areas in equal times. Since the areal velocity (dA/dt) is constant, near perihelion close to the Sun the planet moves fast to fill the same area over a short distance, and at distant aphelion it moves slowly. This is a consequence of the conservation of angular momentum.
3법칙 (조화 법칙): 공전주기 T의 제곱은 긴반지름 a의 세제곱에 비례: 3rd law (harmonic law): The square of the orbital period T is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis a (T² ∝ a³). The larger the orbit, the more than proportionally longer it takes to go around once.
두 부채꼴 넓이는 같다 (같은 시간 동안): The two sectors have the same area (over the same time)
근일점 근처 부채꼴은 짧고 넓적, 원일점 근처는 길고 가늘지만 넓이는 같: The sector near perihelion is short and broad, and the one near aphelion is long and thin, but their areas are equal.
흔한 오개념: \"행성 궤도는 완전한 원이고, 행성은 일정한 속도로 돈다: Common misconception: the idea that "a planet's orbit is a perfect circle and the planet moves at constant speed" was a 2,000-year-old belief that even Ptolemy and Copernicus could not escape. Real orbits are ellipses, and the speed constantly varies. Also, "the Sun is at the center of the ellipse" is a misunderstanding. The Sun is not at the center but at one of the two foci.
행성이 궤도에서 가장 빠르게 움직이는 위치는 어디인가?: Where in its orbit does a planet move fastest?
긴반지름의 양 끝 사이 중간 지점: The midpoint between the two ends of the semi-major axis
케플러 3법칙(T² ∝ a³)에 따르면, 긴반지름 a가 4배인 궤도의 공: According to Kepler's 3rd law (T² ∝ a³), for an orbit whose semi-major axis a is 4 times larger, the orbital period T becomes how many times larger?
독일의 천문학자·수학자로, 천체 관측의 거장 튀코 브라헤(Tycho Br: A German astronomer and mathematician who was an assistant to the master observer Tycho Brahe and inherited his vast observational data after his death. In particular, while trying to fit the orbit of Mars to a circle, he ultimately could not tolerate an error of 8 arcminutes and discovered that the orbit is an ellipse. His persistence over this "8-arcminute discrepancy" is credited with giving birth to the revolution in astronomy.
독실한 신앙과 신비주의적 우주관(『우주의 신비』의 정다면체 모형)을 가졌: Though he held devout faith and a mystical view of the cosmos (the regular-polyhedron model of "Mysterium Cosmographicum"), he submitted thoroughly to observational data. His stance of prioritizing observation over theory, together with Galileo's experimental spirit, shaped the methodology of modern science.
1543년 — 코페르니쿠스 『천구의 회전에 관하여』 출간, 태양중심설 제: 1543 — Copernicus's "On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres" is published, proposing the heliocentric model (though still with circular orbits).
1600년 — 케플러가 프라하에서 튀코 브라헤의 조수가 됨: 1600 — Kepler becomes Tycho Brahe's assistant in Prague.
1601년 — 튀코 사망, 케플러가 정밀 관측 자료를 계승: 1601 — Tycho dies, and Kepler inherits the precise observational data.
1609년 — 『새로운 천문학(Astronomia nova)』 출간, 제: 1609 — "New Astronomy (Astronomia nova)" is published, announcing the 1st and 2nd laws.
1619년 — 『세계의 조화(Harmonices mundi)』 출간, 제: 1619 — "The Harmony of the World (Harmonices mundi)" is published, announcing the 3rd law (T² ∝ a³).
1687년 — 뉴턴이 『프린키피아』에서 만유인력으로 케플러 법칙을 수학적: 1687 — Newton mathematically proves Kepler's laws with universal gravitation in the "Principia."
과학사적 의의: 케플러는 2,000년간 천문학을 지배한 \"완전한 원과: Significance in the history of science: Kepler broke the dogma of "perfect circles and uniform motion" that had dominated astronomy for 2,000 years, and proved with observational data that planetary orbits are ellipses and that speed varies. His three laws later became the decisive foundation on which Newton built the law of universal gravitation, and became the starting point of modern celestial mechanics, which describes the laws of nature quantitatively with observation and mathematics.
공기저항 켜기 (가벼운 물체가 더 늦게 착지): Turn on air resistance (the lighter object lands later)
💡 관찰 포인트: 공기저항을 끈 상태에서 두 물체의 질량을 크게 다르게: 💡 Observation point: With air resistance off, try changing the two objects' masses to be very different. Even with different weights (when air resistance is ignored), the two balls always land at the same time. This is because the acceleration g is independent of mass. Only when you turn on air resistance does the lighter ball fall later.
Understand that in the absence of air resistance, the acceleration of falling is independent of mass.
Learn the position–speed–time relations of uniformly accelerated motion.
낙하시간 t = √(2h/g) 와 착지속도 v = √(2gh) 를 유도·: Derive and apply the fall time t = √(2h/g) and the landing speed v = √(2gh).
Compare how the gravitational acceleration g differs among celestial bodies.
정지 상태에서 자유낙하하는 물체에는 일정한 중력가속도 g가 작용한다. 뉴: An object in free fall from rest experiences a constant gravitational acceleration g. In Newtonian mechanics, the gravity acting on the object is F = m·g, and the acceleration is a = F/m = g. That is, the mass m cancels in numerator and denominator, so the acceleration does not depend on mass at all.
따라서 공기저항이 없는 진공에서는 무거운 쇠공과 가벼운 깃털이 같은 가속: Therefore, in a vacuum with no air resistance, a heavy iron ball and a light feather fall with the same acceleration, and if released together from the same height, they land at the same time.
같은 시각마다 두 공의 높이가 항상 같다. 낙하 거리는 시간의 제곱에 비: At every instant the two balls are always at the same height. The distance fallen is proportional to the square of time.
흔한 오개념: \"무거운 물체가 더 빨리 떨어진다\"는 생각은 아리스토텔: Common misconception: the idea that "heavier objects fall faster" was common sense for 2,000 years since Aristotle. In reality a heavier object experiences a greater force, but its inertia (mass) is correspondingly greater, so the acceleration is the same. In everyday life a feather falls slowly not because of its weight but because of air resistance.
진공(공기저항 없음)에서 무거운 쇠공과 가벼운 깃털을 같은 높이에서 동시: In a vacuum (no air resistance), if you release a heavy iron ball and a light feather together from the same height, what happens?
둘이 동시에 떨어진다: They fall at the same time
지구(g ≈ 9.8 m/s²)에서 높이 19.6 m를 자유낙하할 때 걸리: On Earth (g ≈ 9.8 m/s²), which value is closest to the time t it takes to free-fall from a height of 19.6 m? (t = √(2h/g))
이탈리아 피사 출신의 물리학자·천문학자·수학자로 \"근대 과학의 아버지\: A physicist, astronomer, and mathematician from Pisa, Italy, called "the father of modern science." He established the scientific method combining observation, experiment, and mathematical analysis. With a telescope he observed the moons of Jupiter and the surface of the Moon, and in kinematics he overturned Aristotle's view of motion with free-fall and inclined-plane experiments.
피사의 사탑에서 서로 다른 무게의 공을 떨어뜨려 동시에 착지함을 보였다는: He is famous for the anecdote of dropping balls of different weights from the Leaning Tower of Pisa to show they land at the same time, but this is a story handed down by his student Viviani, and whether the public experiment actually took place is uncertain. Still, it is clear that Galileo reached the same conclusion through thought experiments and inclined-plane experiments.
기원전 4세기 — 아리스토텔레스: \"무거운 물체가 더 빨리 떨어진다\": 4th century BC — Aristotle: establishes the view of motion that "heavier objects fall faster."
1589년경 — 갈릴레오, 피사 대학 교수 시절 낙하 운동 연구 시작 (: c. 1589 — Galileo begins studying falling motion while a professor at the University of Pisa (the setting of the Leaning Tower anecdote).
1604년경 — 경사면 실험으로 낙하 거리가 시간의 제곱에 비례함을 정량: c. 1604 — He quantifies, through inclined-plane experiments, that the distance fallen is proportional to the square of time.
1638년 — 『새로운 두 과학(Discorsi)』 출간, 등가속도 운동: 1638 — "Two New Sciences (Discorsi)" is published, systematizing the laws of uniformly accelerated motion.
1971년 — 아폴로 15호 우주비행사가 달 표면(진공)에서 망치와 깃털: 1971 — An Apollo 15 astronaut verifies it by dropping a hammer and a feather together on the Moon's surface (a vacuum).
과학사적 의의: 2,000년간 의심받지 않던 아리스토텔레스의 권위를 관찰: Significance in the history of science: it was an event that refuted, through observation and experiment, the authority of Aristotle that had gone unquestioned for 2,000 years. The conclusion that "all objects fall with the same acceleration regardless of mass" later led to Newton's laws of motion and gravitation, and, through the equivalence of inertial mass and gravitational mass (the equivalence principle), to Einstein's general theory of relativity. It is a symbol of the Scientific Revolution, showing that experiment, not authority, is the criterion of truth.
시간 간격(0.5초) 마커 표시 — 거리 비 1:3:5:7 확인: Show markers at time intervals (0.5 s) — check the distance ratio 1:3:5:7
0.5초 구간별 이동 거리(홀수 비):: Distance traveled in each 0.5 s interval (odd-number ratio):
💡 관찰 포인트: 마커는 매 0.5초마다 공의 위치에 찍힙니다. 마커 사: 💡 Observation point: A marker is placed at the ball's position every 0.5 s. Notice that the spacing between markers (the distance traveled in each interval) widens in the odd-number ratio 1 : 3 : 5 : 7 … The cumulative distance becomes 1 : 4 : 9 : 16 (the square ratio). Increasing the incline angle θ increases the acceleration a = g·sinθ, so the ball rolls down faster.
Understand that the acceleration on a frictionless incline is a = g·sinθ.
등가속도 운동에서 이동 거리가 시간의 제곱에 비례함(s = ½at²)을: Learn that in uniformly accelerated motion, the distance traveled is proportional to the square of time (s = ½at²).
Discover that the ratio of interval distances over equal time intervals is odd (1:3:5:7…).
Explain why the cumulative distance ratio becomes the square ratio (1:4:9:16).
Compare quantitatively how the incline angle affects the acceleration.
경사면 위의 공에 작용하는 중력 mg 중 경사면 방향 성분은 mg·sin: Of the gravity mg acting on the ball on the incline, the component along the incline is mg·sinθ. Ignoring friction, from Newton's second law ma = mg·sinθ the mass m cancels, so the acceleration is determined as a = g·sinθ. That is, the acceleration depends only on the incline angle.
정지 상태에서 출발하므로 등가속도 운동이고, 이동 거리는 s = ½·a·: Since it starts from rest, the motion is uniformly accelerated, and the distance traveled is s = ½·a·t², proportional to the square of time. In an era when time could not be measured precisely, Galileo used an incline to make the fall 'slow' and thereby discovered this square relationship.
홀수 법칙: 같은 시간 간격 Δt로 끊어 보면 n번째 구간의 이동 거리는: The odd-number law: dividing the motion into equal time intervals Δt, the distance traveled in the n-th interval is proportional to ½a(Δt)²·(2n−1). Therefore the interval-distance ratio becomes the odd-number ratio 1 : 3 : 5 : 7 …, and the cumulative distance ratio from the start becomes the square ratio 1 : 4 : 9 : 16.
같은 시간 간격(빨간 마커)마다 공이 더 멀리 간다. 구간 거리 비 1:: At each equal time interval (red markers), the ball travels farther. Interval-distance ratio 1:3:5:7, cumulative-distance ratio 1:4:9:16.
흔한 오개념: \"공이 일정한 속도로 내려간다\" 또는 \"같은 시간이면: Common misconception: it is easy to think "the ball descends at a constant speed" or "it travels the same distance in the same time." In reality, because it is uniformly accelerated motion, the speed increases over time, so the distance covered in the same time grows steadily (1:3:5:7…). Distance is proportional not to time but to the square of time.
마찰을 무시할 때 경사각 θ를 더 크게 하면 경사면 가속도 a = g·s: When friction is ignored, if you increase the incline angle θ, the incline acceleration a = g·sinθ becomes?
정지 상태에서 출발한 공을 같은 시간 간격으로 끊어 볼 때, 각 구간의: When a ball starting from rest is divided into equal time intervals, what is the ratio of distances traveled in each interval?
이탈리아 피사 출신의 물리학자·천문학자·수학자로 \"근대 과학의 아버지\: A physicist, astronomer, and mathematician from Pisa, Italy, called "the father of modern science." In an era without precise clocks, he devised an ingenious method of using an incline to make falling 'slow' in order to measure falling motion directly. He rolled a bronze ball down a smoothly finished groove and, timing it with a water clock (the weight of the water that flowed out), quantified the relationship between distance and time.
『새로운 두 과학(Discorsi, 1638)』에서 갈릴레오는 이 실험을: In "Two New Sciences (Discorsi, 1638)," Galileo described this experiment in detail and clearly showed that the distance traveled is proportional to the square of time and that the distance ratio over equal time intervals is odd (1:3:5…).
기원전 4세기 — 아리스토텔레스: 무거운 물체가 더 빨리, 일정한 속도로: 4th century BC — Aristotle: the view of motion that heavier objects fall faster, at a constant speed.
1604년경 — 갈릴레오, 파도바 시절 경사면 실험으로 거리–시간 제곱: c. 1604 — Galileo discovers the distance–time-square law through inclined-plane experiments during his time in Padua.
1610년 — 『별의 전령(Sidereus Nuncius)』으로 천문 관: 1610 — He announces his astronomical observational results in "The Starry Messenger (Sidereus Nuncius)."
1638년 — 『새로운 두 과학』 출간, 경사면 실험과 등가속도 운동 법: 1638 — "Two New Sciences" is published, systematizing the inclined-plane experiment and the laws of uniformly accelerated motion.
1687년 — 뉴턴 『프린키피아』, 갈릴레오의 운동학을 역학 법칙으로 일: 1687 — Newton's "Principia" generalizes Galileo's kinematics into the laws of mechanics.
과학사적 의의: 측정 도구의 한계를 '경사면으로 낙하를 늦추는' 실험 설: Significance in the history of science: it became a model of quantitative experiment in that he overcame the limits of measuring instruments with an experimental design that 'slowed the fall with an incline.' The discovery that "distance is proportional to the square of time" made the mathematical description of uniformly accelerated motion possible and later led to Newton's laws of motion. It is a leading example of the Scientific Revolution, describing nature with measurement and mathematics rather than authority.
💡 관찰 포인트: 4개의 위성(이오·유로파·가니메데·칼리스토)이 각자 다: 💡 Observation point: The four moons (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto) orbit Jupiter each with a different period. Compare the orbits seen from above (left) with the apparent positions seen from Earth (the small dots on either side of Jupiter). The moons oscillate left and right about Jupiter, and their arrangement changes each day. This means that moons orbiting a body other than Earth (Jupiter) exist — direct evidence refuting the geocentric model in which everything orbits Earth.
굴절망원경의 배율이 두 렌즈의 초점거리 비 M = fobj / feye: Understand that the magnification of a refracting telescope is set by the ratio of the two lenses' focal lengths, M = f_obj / f_eye.
Confirm by observation that Jupiter's four major moons orbit with different periods.
지구에서는 궤도를 옆에서 보므로 위성이 목성 양옆으로 일렬로 진동해 보임: Explain that because from Earth we see the orbits edge-on, the moons appear to oscillate in a line on either side of Jupiter.
Argue how the discovery of "bodies orbiting Jupiter" refutes the geocentric model.
갈릴레오가 만든 굴절망원경은 빛을 모으는 대물렌즈와 눈으로 보는 접안렌즈: The refracting telescope Galileo built consists of an objective lens that gathers light and an eyepiece for viewing with the eye. The angular magnification for viewing a distant body enlarged is determined by the ratio of the two lenses' focal lengths. The longer the objective's focal length f_obj and the shorter the eyepiece's focal length f_eye, the greater the magnification.
이오·유로파·가니메데·칼리스토는 각각 약 1.8 / 3.6 / 7.2 /: Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto orbit Jupiter with periods of about 1.8 / 3.6 / 7.2 / 16.7 days, respectively. Because we see these orbits almost edge-on (in the plane), the circular motion is projected onto a horizontal axis, so the moons appear to line up on either side of Jupiter and oscillate left and right. That is why the line-up of the moons differs from night to night.
목성 양옆 일렬: In a line on either side of Jupiter
원궤도(왼쪽)를 옆에서 보면, 위성은 목성을 중심으로 양옆으로 진동하는: Seeing the circular orbits (left) edge-on, the moons appear as points oscillating from side to side about Jupiter (right).
흔한 오개념: \"망원경 배율은 무조건 높을수록 좋다\"고 생각하기 쉽다: Common misconception: it is easy to think "the higher the telescope magnification, the better." In reality, increasing magnification narrows the field of view, dims the image, and magnifies hand-shake and atmospheric turbulence along with it, making the image blurrier instead. Also, rather than "the moons move away from and toward Jupiter," the accurate interpretation is that we see the circular orbits edge-on, so they appear to oscillate side to side.
대물렌즈 초점거리 100 cm, 접안렌즈 초점거리 5 cm인 굴절망원경의: What is the magnification M of a refracting telescope with an objective focal length of 100 cm and an eyepiece focal length of 5 cm?
목성의 위성 발견이 천동설(지구중심설)에 준 충격은 무엇인가?: What impact did the discovery of Jupiter's moons have on the geocentric model (Earth-centered theory)?
지구가 태양보다 크다는 것을 보였다: It showed that Earth is larger than the Sun
지구가 아닌 천체(목성)를 도는 천체가 있음을 보여 천동설을 약화시켰다: It showed that there are bodies orbiting a body other than Earth (Jupiter), weakening the geocentric model
모든 행성이 정확한 원궤도를 돈다는 것을 증명했다: It proved that all planets move in exact circular orbits
이탈리아 피사 출신의 물리학자·천문학자·수학자로 \"근대 과학의 아버지\: A physicist, astronomer, and mathematician from Pisa, Italy, called "the father of modern science." Hearing news of the telescope invented in the Netherlands in 1609, he personally improved its performance to build a refracting telescope magnifying up to about 20×, and became the first serious observer to point it at the sky.
1610년 1월, 목성 곁에서 일렬로 늘어선 작은 별 같은 점들이 밤마다: In January 1610, he observed small star-like dots lined up beside Jupiter changing position night after night, and realized these were moons orbiting Jupiter. These four moons are today called the "Galilean moons." He announced the observations of that same year in "The Starry Messenger (Sidereus Nuncius)."
2세기 — 프톨레마이오스, 모든 천체가 지구를 돈다는 천동설을 집대성: 2nd century — Ptolemy compiles the geocentric model in which all bodies orbit Earth.
1543년 — 코페르니쿠스, 태양중심설(지동설)을 담은 『천구의 회전에: 1543 — Copernicus publishes "On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres," containing the heliocentric model.
1608년 — 네덜란드에서 망원경(스파이글라스) 발명: 1608 — The telescope (spyglass) is invented in the Netherlands.
1609년 — 갈릴레오, 망원경을 개량·제작하여 천체 관측 시작: 1609 — Galileo improves and builds a telescope and begins astronomical observation.
1610년 1월 — 목성의 4대 위성 발견, 3월 『별의 전령』 출간: January 1610 — He discovers Jupiter's four major moons; in March "The Starry Messenger" is published.
1633년 — 종교재판에서 지동설 옹호로 유죄 판결, 가택연금: 1633 — He is found guilty at the Inquisition for advocating the heliocentric model and placed under house arrest.
과학사적 의의: 목성을 도는 위성의 발견은 \"모든 천체는 지구를 중심으: Significance in the history of science: the discovery of moons orbiting Jupiter was decisive observational evidence that directly toppled the core premise of the geocentric model, that "all bodies orbit Earth." By showing that a body other than Earth could have its own moons, it lent powerful support to Copernicus's heliocentric model and became a symbolic event of the Scientific Revolution, in which telescopic observation rather than authority (Aristotle, Ptolemy) became the criterion of truth.
💡 관찰 포인트: 백색광 한 줄기가 프리즘을 지나면 빨주노초파남보로 갈라: 💡 Observation point: When a single beam of white light passes through a prism, it splits into red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. White light is actually a combination of many colors (wavelengths) of light, and because the refractive index in glass differs for each wavelength, violet (short wavelength) bends more than red (long wavelength). Increasing the dispersion strength spreads the colors more widely in a fan, and increasing the apex angle increases the overall deflection.
Understand that white light is a combination of light of many wavelengths.
Explain, with Snell's law, the principle by which light bends at the boundary of a medium.
굴절률이 파장에 따라 달라지는 분산(dispersion) 때문에 색이 갈: Know that the colors split because of dispersion — the refractive index varies with wavelength.
Explain why violet (short wavelength) is refracted more than red (long wavelength).
빛이 공기에서 유리로 들어갈 때 속도가 느려지며 경계면에서 꺾인다(굴절): When light passes from air into glass, its speed slows and it bends at the interface (refraction). The degree of bending is determined by Snell's law, n₁ sinθ₁ = n₂ sinθ₂. The refractive index n of glass varies with the wavelength of light: the shorter the wavelength, the larger the refractive index and the more it bends. This is called dispersion (chromatic aberration).
백색광은 빨강부터 보라까지 모든 파장이 섞여 있다. 프리즘의 두 경사면을: White light contains all wavelengths from red to violet. Passing through the two slanted faces of the prism, each wavelength is refracted at a slightly different angle, so it ultimately fans out into the continuous spectrum of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. The wavelength-dependent refractive index is well fit by the Cauchy approximation n(λ) = A + B / λ² (e.g., in ordinary glass, violet n ≈ 1.53, red n ≈ 1.51).
흔한 오개념: \"프리즘(유리)이 백색광에 색을 입혀 만들어낸다\"고 생: Common misconception: it is easy to think "the prism (glass) adds color to white light and creates it." In reality the colors are all present in the white light from the start, and the prism merely separates and displays them by the difference in refraction per wavelength. Newton proved this by showing that recombining the split light with a second prism produces white light again.

굴절률이 파장에 따라 달라지기 때문 (분산): Because the refractive index varies with wavelength (dispersion)
유리가 색을 새로 만들어내기 때문: Because the glass newly creates color
빛이 프리즘 안에서 반사되기 때문: Because light reflects inside the prism
영국의 물리학자·수학자·천문학자로, 만유인력과 운동 법칙을 정립한 고전역: An English physicist, mathematician, and astronomer, the completer of classical mechanics who established universal gravitation and the laws of motion. When Cambridge was closed by the plague in 1665–1666, he stayed in his hometown of Woolsthorpe and poured out core discoveries in calculus, universal gravitation, and light and color (the so-called "miracle years"). Through prism experiments he revealed that white light is a combination of many colors, and compiled this in his 1704 work "Opticks."
1637년 — 데카르트·스넬, 굴절의 법칙(스넬의 법칙)을 정식화: 1637 — Descartes and Snell formulate the law of refraction (Snell's law).
1665~1666년 — 뉴턴, 흑사병 피난기에 프리즘으로 빛의 분산을 실: 1665–1666 — Newton experiments with the dispersion of light using a prism during his plague refuge ("the miracle years").
1672년 — 「빛과 색의 새 이론」을 왕립학회에 발표, 백색광이 색의: 1672 — He presents "A New Theory about Light and Colours" to the Royal Society, arguing that white light is a combination of colors.
1704년 — 「광학(Opticks)」 출간, 분산·반사·간섭 관찰을 집: 1704 — "Opticks" is published, compiling observations of dispersion, reflection, and interference.
1814년 — 프라운호퍼가 태양 스펙트럼의 흡수선을 발견해 분광학의 길을: 1814 — Fraunhofer discovers absorption lines in the solar spectrum, opening the way to spectroscopy.
1859년 — 키르히호프·분젠, 분광으로 원소를 식별하며 분광학을 확립: 1859 — Kirchhoff and Bunsen establish spectroscopy by identifying elements through spectra.
과학사적 의의: 뉴턴은 색이 빛의 본질적 성질이며 백색광이 모든 색의 혼: Significance in the history of science: Newton proved experimentally that color is an intrinsic property of light and that white light is a mixture of all colors, overturning the prevailing belief of the time that glass or objects "add" color. This dispersion experiment later led to spectroscopy and became a powerful tool of modern science — analyzing the composition of stars, studying spectral lines in quantum mechanics, and more.
💡 관찰 포인트: 포탄은 매 순간 지구로 떨어지고 있습니다. 다만 수평: 💡 Observation point: The cannonball is falling toward Earth at every moment. But if the horizontal speed is fast enough, the Earth's surface curves away by just as much as the cannonball falls, so it never reaches the ground. This is exactly an orbit. A satellite does not "not fall" — it "keeps falling while curving past Earth."
Understand that orbital motion is simply "free fall thrown fast in the horizontal direction."
발사 속도에 따라 추락 → 타원궤도 → 원궤도 → 탈출로 갈리는 경계를: Know the boundaries at which the launch speed divides fall → elliptical orbit → circular orbit → escape.
원궤도 속도 vorbit = √(g·R) 와 탈출속도 vescape =: Learn the circular-orbit speed v_orbit = √(g·R) and the escape speed v_escape = √2·v_orbit.
Accept that gravity governs planets, satellites, and cannonballs by the same law (universal gravitation).
높은 산 위 대포에서 포탄을 수평으로 쏘면, 포탄은 중력 때문에 아래로: If you fire a cannonball horizontally from a cannon atop a high mountain, the cannonball curves downward due to gravity and eventually falls to the ground. The faster the launch speed, the farther it flies and the more distant the point where it lands.
속도를 계속 높이면, 포탄이 한 순간 떨어지는 거리만큼 둥근 지구 표면도: If you keep increasing the speed, the round Earth's surface recedes by just as much as the cannonball falls in a given moment. Eventually the cannonball never reaches the ground and enters a circular orbit around Earth. This speed is the circular-orbit speed v_orbit = √(g·R). Faster than this it becomes an elliptical orbit, and at or above the escape speed v_escape = √2·v_orbit it escapes Earth's gravity and does not return.
지표 부근(R ≈ 6,371 km, g ≈ 9.8 m/s²)에서 vorb: Near the surface (R ≈ 6,371 km, g ≈ 9.8 m/s²), v_orbit ≈ 7.9 km/s and v_escape ≈ 11.2 km/s.
같은 발사점, 같은 수평 방향. 속도만 다를 뿐인데 추락·타원·원궤도로: Same launch point, same horizontal direction. Only the speed differs, yet it divides into fall, ellipse, and circular orbit.
흔한 오개념: \"인공위성은 지구 중력이 닿지 않는 곳에 있어서 떨어지지: Common misconception: the idea that "a satellite does not fall because it is where Earth's gravity does not reach" is wrong. Even in low orbit (altitude ~400 km), gravity acts at about 89% of its surface value, almost unchanged. A satellite has not escaped gravity — it is continuously in free fall. It is just that its horizontal speed is very fast (about 7.7 km/s), so the curve of its fall matches Earth's curvature and it never reaches the ground. That is why inside a satellite there is not "zero gravity" but a state of free fall (a state in which weight is not felt).
인공위성이 지구로 떨어지지 않는(궤도를 도는) 이유로 가장 옳은 것은?: Which is the most correct reason a satellite does not fall to Earth (stays in orbit)?
그 높이에는 지구 중력이 미치지 않기 때문: Because Earth's gravity does not reach that altitude
원심력이 중력보다 커서 바깥으로 밀려나기 때문: Because the centrifugal force is greater than gravity and pushes it outward
계속 자유낙하하지만 수평 속도가 충분해 지구 곡률을 따라 돌기 때문: Because it keeps free-falling, but its horizontal speed is enough to go around following Earth's curvature
원궤도 속도가 vorbit일 때, 지구 중력을 벗어나기 위한 탈출속도 v: When the circular-orbit speed is v_orbit, what is the escape speed v_escape needed to escape Earth's gravity?
영국의 물리학자·수학자·천문학자로 고전역학의 체계를 완성했다. 운동의 세: An English physicist, mathematician, and astronomer who completed the system of classical mechanics. Through the three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation, he explained the fall of an apple, the orbit of the Moon, and the motion of planets with a single law. He independently invented calculus, and also left great achievements in optics — the nature of light and color, the reflecting telescope, and more.
대포 사고실험은 뉴턴의 유작 『세계의 체계(A Treatise of th: The cannon thought experiment became widely known as an illustration in Newton's posthumous work "A Treatise of the System of the World." Through a figure of a cannonball fired ever faster from atop a high mountain (labeled V, D, E, F, G) eventually going once around Earth, it intuitively showed that the Moon orbiting Earth and a cannonball falling follow the same principle.
1609~1619년 — 케플러, 행성 운동의 세 법칙을 관측으로 정리: 1609–1619 — Kepler organizes the three laws of planetary motion from observation.
1666년경 — 뉴턴, \"기적의 해\"에 중력과 운동에 관한 착상을 얻: c. 1666 — Newton gets ideas about gravity and motion in his "miracle years" (the apple anecdote).
1687년 — 『프린키피아(Principia)』 출간, 운동 법칙과 만유: 1687 — The "Principia" is published, announcing the laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation.
1728년 — 사후 출간된 『세계의 체계』에 대포 사고실험 삽화 수록: 1728 — The cannon thought experiment illustration is included in the posthumously published "A Treatise of the System of the World."
1957년 — 스푸트니크 1호 발사, 뉴턴의 사고실험이 실제 인공위성으로: 1957 — Sputnik 1 is launched, realizing Newton's thought experiment as an actual satellite.
과학사적 의의: 대포 사고실험은 \"하늘의 운동\"과 \"땅의 운동\"을: Significance in the history of science: the cannon thought experiment is the decisive insight that unified "the motion of the heavens" and "the motion of the earth" into one. Breaking the ancient belief that celestial bodies follow a sacred, separate law, it showed that even the Moon's orbit is explained by the same universal gravitation as the fall of a cannonball. This idea was realized 270 years later in satellites and space flight, and became the starting point of modern celestial mechanics and astronautics.

💡 관찰 포인트: 두 물체는 서로를 같은 크기의 힘으로 끌어당긴다(작용–: 💡 Observation point: The two objects attract each other with forces of equal magnitude (action–reaction). If you double the distance r, the force decreases to 1/4 (inverse square); if you halve it, it becomes 4 times. Doubling the mass exactly doubles the force. Watch together how the arrow lengths and the point on the 1/r² graph at the top right change.
Understand the universality that any two objects with mass attract each other.
Explain that the attraction is proportional to the product of the two masses (double the mass → double the force).
인력이 거리의 제곱에 반비례함(역제곱 법칙)을 설명한다(거리 2배 → 힘: Explain that the attraction is inversely proportional to the square of the distance (the inverse-square law) (double the distance → 1/4 the force).
중력 상수 G의 의미와 식 F = G·m₁·m₂ / r² 의 각 항을 해: Interpret the meaning of the gravitational constant G and each term in the formula F = G·m₁·m₂ / r².
Understand the unifying view that the apple on the ground and the Moon in the heavens follow the same law.
질량을 가진 모든 두 물체는 서로를 끌어당긴다. 이 힘의 크기는 두 물체: Any two objects with mass attract each other. The magnitude of this force is proportional to the product of the two objects' masses m₁·m₂ and inversely proportional to the square of the distance r² between them. The constant of proportionality is the universal gravitational constant G (= 6.674×10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²).
거리가 핵심이다. 거리를 2배로 하면 분모가 2² = 4배가 되어 힘은: Distance is the key. Doubling the distance makes the denominator 2² = 4 times larger, so the force decreases to 1/4. Tripling it reduces it to 1/9. This is called the inverse-square law. The two forces are always equal in magnitude and opposite in direction (toward each other), so even a small object attracts a large object with the same force.
흔한 오개념: \"무거운 물체가 가벼운 물체를 더 세게 끌어당기고, 가벼: Common misconception: it is easy to think "a heavy object attracts a light object more strongly, and the light object attracts more weakly." In reality the magnitudes of the forces the two objects exert on each other are exactly equal (action–reaction). The force with which Earth attracts an apple and the force with which the apple attracts Earth are equal in magnitude. The lighter one accelerates more not because the force differs but because its mass is small (a = F/m).

2. 거리는 그대로 두고 한 물체의 질량만 2배로 하면 만유인력은?: 2. If you keep the distance the same but double the mass of one object, what happens to the universal gravitation?
2배로 커진다 (질량에 비례): It becomes 2 times larger (proportional to mass)
영국의 물리학자·수학자·천문학자. 운동의 3법칙과 만유인력 법칙을 세워: An English physicist, mathematician, and astronomer. He completed classical mechanics by establishing the three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation, and with the same principle explained the elliptical orbits of planets (Kepler's laws) and falling motion on the ground as one. He invented calculus, and also left his name through optical research on light and color and the construction of a reflecting telescope. In 1687 he published "Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy (Principia)," compiling the Scientific Revolution.
1543년 — 코페르니쿠스가 지동설을 발표(태양 중심 우주): 1543 — Copernicus announces the heliocentric model (a Sun-centered universe).
1609~1619년 — 케플러가 행성 운동 3법칙을 정리(타원 궤도): 1609–1619 — Kepler organizes the three laws of planetary motion (elliptical orbits).
1610년 — 갈릴레오가 망원경으로 목성의 위성 등을 관측, 지동설을 뒷: 1610 — Galileo observes Jupiter's moons and more with a telescope, supporting the heliocentric model.
1665~1666년 — 뉴턴이 페스트로 고향에 머물며 중력·미적분·광학의: 1665–1666 — Newton, staying in his hometown due to the plague, gets the core ideas of gravity, calculus, and optics (the apple anecdote).
1684년 — 핼리의 권유로 행성 운동의 수학적 증명에 착수: 1684 — At Halley's urging, he begins the mathematical proof of planetary motion.
1687년 — 「프린키피아」 출간, 만유인력 법칙과 운동 법칙을 발표: 1687 — The "Principia" is published, announcing the law of universal gravitation and the laws of motion.
1798년 — 캐번디시가 비틀림 저울 실험으로 G를 측정, 지구의 질량을: 1798 — Cavendish measures G with a torsion-balance experiment and calculates the mass of Earth.
과학사적 의의: 만유인력 법칙은 떨어지는 사과(지상)와 도는 달(천상)을: Significance in the history of science: the law of universal gravitation bound the falling apple (on the ground) and the orbiting Moon (in the heavens) into one and the same law, toppling the long-held belief that heaven and earth moved by different principles. With this, Kepler's planetary laws were mathematically derived, and the modern scientific worldview that nature follows universal, mathematical laws was established. This framework was the foundation of physics for over 200 years, and remained the standard for predicting celestial motion until Einstein's general theory of relativity later extended it with a more precise explanation.
💡 관찰 포인트: 피스톤을 눌러 부피 V를 절반으로 줄이면 압력 P는 정: 💡 Observation point: If you press the piston to reduce the volume V by half, the pressure P becomes exactly 2 times. The smaller the volume, the denser the gas particles and the more often they strike the walls, so the pressure gauge needle rises. Conversely, increasing the volume scatters the particles and lowers the pressure. Throughout, the product P · V stays constant.
일정한 온도에서 기체의 압력과 부피가 반비례함(P ∝ 1/V)을 이해한다: Understand that at constant temperature the pressure and volume of a gas are inversely proportional (P ∝ 1/V).
Explain the meaning of the relation P · V = constant (k).
Interpret, with a particle model, that when the volume decreases, particle collisions become more frequent and the pressure increases.
Know that Boyle's law holds only when the temperature and the amount of gas are fixed.
밀폐된 실린더 속 기체 입자들은 끊임없이 움직이며 벽에 부딪힌다. 이 충: Gas particles in a sealed cylinder move ceaselessly and strike the walls. The force per unit area created by these collisions is the pressure. If you reduce the volume with the piston while keeping the temperature and the amount of gas fixed, the same number of particles are confined in a narrower space and strike the walls more often. As a result the pressure increases.
Halving the volume doubles the collision frequency, so the pressure doubles. That is, the pressure is inversely proportional to the volume, and their product is always a constant k: P · V = k. This is Boyle's law.
흔한 오개념: \"부피를 줄이면 기체 입자 자체가 작아지거나 사라진다\": Common misconception: it is easy to think "reducing the volume makes the gas particles themselves smaller or disappear." In reality the number and size of the particles stay the same; they merely gather in a narrower space and collide more often. Also, Boyle's law holds only when the temperature is constant. If the temperature changes, the pressure–volume relationship changes too.
1. 온도가 일정할 때 기체의 부피를 1/2로 줄이면 압력은 어떻게 되는: 1. When the temperature is constant, if you reduce the volume of a gas to 1/2, what happens to the pressure?
2. 보일의 법칙 P · V = k 에서 일정하게 유지되는 것은 무엇인가: 2. In Boyle's law P · V = k, what is kept constant?
압력과 부피의 곱 P · V: The product of pressure and volume, P · V
아일랜드 출신의 자연철학자·화학자·물리학자로, 근대 화학의 아버지로 불린: An Irish-born natural philosopher, chemist, and physicist, called the father of modern chemistry. Together with his assistant Robert Hooke, he improved the vacuum pump to experiment precisely on the properties of gases, and by pouring mercury into a J-shaped glass tube to trap air, he quantitatively measured the relationship between pressure and volume. In his work "The Sceptical Chymist" (1661), he criticized the four-element theory of alchemy and laid the foundation of modern chemistry based on experiment and measurement.
1643년 — 토리첼리가 수은 기압계를 발명하여 대기압의 존재를 입증: 1643 — Torricelli invents the mercury barometer, proving the existence of atmospheric pressure.
1654년 — 게리케가 마그데부르크 반구 실험으로 진공과 대기압의 힘을: 1654 — Guericke demonstrates the force of a vacuum and atmospheric pressure with the Magdeburg hemispheres experiment.
1659년 — 보일과 훅이 진공 펌프를 개량해 기체 실험을 시작: 1659 — Boyle and Hooke improve the vacuum pump and begin gas experiments.
1662년 — 보일이 압력과 부피의 반비례 관계(보일의 법칙)를 발표: 1662 — Boyle announces the inverse relationship between pressure and volume (Boyle's law).
1676년 — 마리오트가 독립적으로 같은 관계를 확인(유럽에서 마리오트: 1676 — Mariotte independently confirms the same relationship (also called Mariotte's law in Europe).
1787년 — 샤를이 온도-부피 관계를 밝혀 이상기체 법칙으로 이어짐: 1787 — Charles reveals the temperature–volume relationship, leading to the ideal gas law.
과학사적 의의: 보일의 법칙은 기체의 거동을 수식으로 표현한 최초의 정량: Significance in the history of science: Boyle's law is one of the first quantitative laws to express the behavior of a gas in a formula, a model case showing the modern scientific method of treating natural phenomena with measurement and mathematics. It later combined with Charles's law and Gay-Lussac's law to develop into the ideal gas equation of state (PV = nRT), and became the starting point of the kinetic theory of gases, which treats the motion of gas particles.

So Cavendish hung a rod on a hair-thin wire to amplify this minute force into a torsion angle and read it. Doubling the distance r reduces the attraction to 1/4 (inverse square). Increasing M or m increases both the attraction and the deflection angle together. Watch the rod be pulled slightly toward the large balls and twist.
만유인력 법칙 F = G·M·m / r² 에서 각 변수가 인력에 주는 영: Explain how each variable in the law of universal gravitation F = G·M·m / r² affects the attraction.
Understand that the attraction varies with the inverse square of the distance r (1/r²).
비틀림 저울이 아주 작은 힘을 비틀림 각으로 증폭해 측정하는 원리를 안다: Know the principle by which a torsion balance amplifies a very small force into a torsion angle to measure it.
Grasp how the gravitational constant G and Earth's mass are obtained from the measured attraction.
두 질량 사이에는 만유인력이 작용한다. 그 크기는 두 질량의 곱에 비례하: Universal gravitation acts between two masses. Its magnitude is proportional to the product of the two masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance: F = G·M·m / r². Here G is the gravitational constant common to all objects.
The problem is that the attraction between everyday objects is too small to measure directly. Cavendish hung small lead balls (m) on both ends of a light rod, suspended on a thin metal wire (fiber), and brought heavy lead balls (M) alongside them. When the minute attraction twists the rod, the twist balances against the restoring torque of the suspension wire trying to return to its original state. At equilibrium the torsion angle θ is proportional to the attraction F, so by precisely reading θ from the movement of a light spot reflected in a mirror, F can be found in reverse.
F를 알면 F = G·M·m / r² 에서 G를 구할 수 있고, 지표면: If F is known, G can be obtained from F = G·M·m / r², and from the surface gravitational acceleration g and Earth's radius R, even Earth's mass M⊕ = g·R² / G is calculated. Cavendish's original goal was precisely "weighing the Earth."
r = M와 m 중심 거리: r = center distance between M and m
흔한 오개념: \"캐번디시 실험은 G를 잰 것이 아니라 지구 무게를 잰: Common misconception: people tend to argue that "the Cavendish experiment did not measure G but weighed Earth," or conversely that "it directly measured G." In fact Cavendish himself did not explicitly use the constant G but obtained the mean density of Earth. However, because today's G and Earth's mass are calculated directly from the attraction he measured, in modern terms it is called "the experiment that first made G measurable." One more thing, the attraction is stronger the larger the mass, but distance is the key, so even a slight reduction in r sharply increases the attraction (inverse square).

An English chemist and physicist, famous for his extremely introverted and reclusive character. He inherited an enormous fortune but devoted himself solely to research, and much of his work was not published, so its true value was often known only after his death. He isolated hydrogen ("inflammable air") and clarified its properties, and contributed to showing that water is not an element but a compound. In 1798, at age 67, he refined a torsion-balance apparatus devised and left behind by John Michell to measure the attraction between two lead balls in the "weighing the Earth" experiment.
1687년 — 뉴턴이 「프린키피아」에서 만유인력 법칙을 제시(상수 G의: 1687 — Newton presents the law of universal gravitation in the "Principia" (the value of the constant G unknown).
1772년경 — 존 미첼(John Michell)이 비틀림 저울 장치를: c. 1772 — John Michell designs the torsion-balance apparatus (dies before completing it).
1797~1798년 — 캐번디시가 장치를 물려받아 개량하고 미세 인력을: 1797–1798 — Cavendish inherits the apparatus, refines it, and measures the minute attraction.
1798년 — 「지구 밀도를 결정하는 실험」 논문 발표, 지구 평균 밀도: 1798 — He publishes the paper "Experiments to Determine the Density of the Earth," computing Earth's mean density as about 5.45 times.
1873년 — 코르뉘 등 후대 학자들이 결과로부터 G ≈ 6.7×10⁻¹: 1873 — Later scholars such as Cornu organize the result into the form G ≈ 6.7×10⁻¹¹.
현재 — G = 6.674×10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg² (가장 정밀도가 낮: Present — G = 6.674×10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg² (one of the least precisely known fundamental constants).
과학사적 의의: 캐번디시 실험은 실험실 안의 평범한 물체 사이에서 만유인: Significance in the history of science: the Cavendish experiment is the first to directly measure universal gravitation between ordinary objects in a laboratory. From its result, the mass and density of Earth, and further the masses of the Sun and planets, could be calculated. It set the standard for precision measurement of nanonewton-scale minute forces with a torsion balance, and this method soon led to Coulomb's measurement of the electric force. It is regarded as the event that "placed on a scale" an Earth whose weight could not be known.

💡 관찰 포인트: 두 전하의 부호가 같으면(둘 다 +이거나 둘 다 −): 💡 Observation point: If the two charges have the same sign (both + or both −), they repel each other (repulsion), and the arrows point outward. If the signs differ, they attract each other (attraction), and the arrows face each other. Doubling the distance r reduces the force to 1/4 (inversely proportional to the square of the distance); increasing the charge increases the force and lengthens the arrows.
두 점전하 사이 힘이 F = k·q₁·q₂ / r² 로 주어짐을 이해한다: Understand that the force between two point charges is given by F = k·q₁·q₂ / r².
Explain that the force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance r (the inverse-square law).
Know that like-sign charges repel and opposite-sign charges attract.
Grasp that the force is proportional to the product of the two charges.
Compare the point that it has the same form (inverse square) as the law of universal gravitation.
정지한 두 점전하 사이에는 전기력이 작용한다. 그 크기는 두 전하량(q₁: An electric force acts between two stationary point charges. Its magnitude is proportional to the product of the two charges (q₁, q₂) and inversely proportional to the square of the distance (r) between them. This is called Coulomb's law.
비례상수 k ≈ 8.99 × 10⁹ N·m²/C² 는 쿨롱 상수다(진공: The constant of proportionality k ≈ 8.99 × 10⁹ N·m²/C² is Coulomb's constant (in vacuum). The direction of the force is determined by the sign of the charges: like signs repel each other (repulsion), and unlike signs attract each other (attraction). The forces on the two charges are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction (action–reaction).
흔한 오개념: \"거리를 2배로 멀리하면 힘도 절반(1/2)이 된다\"고: Common misconception: it is easy to think "if you double the distance, the force also halves (1/2)." In reality it is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, so doubling the distance makes the force 1/4. There is also the misunderstanding that "a large charge pushes a small charge more strongly," but the forces the two charges exert on each other are always equal in magnitude (the action–reaction law).

과학자: 샤를 드 쿨롱 (Charles-Augustin de Coulom: Scientist: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb (Charles-Augustin de Coulomb, 1736–1806)
프랑스의 물리학자·군사 공학자. 본래 요새와 토목 공사를 담당한 공병 장: A French physicist and military engineer. Originally an engineering officer in charge of fortifications and civil works, he gained fame for precise measurement studies of friction and torsion. With a torsion balance he devised himself, he quantitatively measured very small electric forces and, in 1785, proved experimentally that the electric force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance. The unit of charge, the coulomb (C), is named after him.
1600년 — 길버트가 「자석에 관하여(De Magnete)」에서 전기·: 1600 — Gilbert systematically studies electric and magnetic phenomena in "On the Magnet (De Magnete)."
1687년 — 뉴턴이 만유인력의 역제곱 법칙(F ∝ 1/r²)을 제시: 1687 — Newton presents the inverse-square law of universal gravitation (F ∝ 1/r²).
1767년 — 프리스틀리가 전기력도 역제곱일 것이라 추측(정성적): 1767 — Priestley conjectures that the electric force is also inverse-square (qualitatively).
1785년 — 쿨롱이 비틀림 저울로 전기력의 역제곱 법칙을 정밀하게 측정: 1785 — Coulomb precisely measures and announces the inverse-square law of the electric force with a torsion balance.
1830년대~ — 가우스·맥스웰을 거쳐 전자기학의 수학적 기초로 발전: 1830s onward — Through Gauss and Maxwell, it develops into the mathematical foundation of electromagnetism.
1909년 — 밀리컨의 기름방울 실험으로 기본 전하량 e 측정, 쿨롱 법: 1909 — Millikan's oil-drop experiment measures the elementary charge e, quantifying the foundation of Coulomb's law.
과학사적 의의: 쿨롱의 법칙은 전기 현상을 정량적·수학적으로 다룬 최초의: Significance in the history of science: Coulomb's law is the first achievement to treat electrical phenomena quantitatively and mathematically, turning electricity — once merely a vague object of observation — into a measurable physical quantity. That it has the same form as the inverse-square law of gravity became a clue showing the unity of the laws of nature, and it became the starting point of all electromagnetism, leading later to Gauss's law and Maxwell's equations.
금속쌍 선택 (전극 전위차 → 셀당 전압): Choose a metal pair (electrode potential difference → voltage per cell)
💡 관찰 포인트: 셀(층)을 많이 쌓을수록 더미가 높아지고 전압계 바늘이: 💡 Observation point: The more cells (layers) you stack, the taller the pile and the higher the voltmeter needle rises. The total voltage is directly proportional to the number of cells n (total voltage = n × voltage per cell). Changing the metal pair changes the voltage per cell, so the total voltage changes even for the same number of layers. The significance of the voltaic pile is that it is humanity's first source of continuous current.
서로 다른 두 금속과 전해질로 이루어진 한 셀이 일정한 기전력(전압)을: Understand that one cell made of two different metals and an electrolyte produces a constant electromotive force (voltage).
셀(층)을 직렬로 쌓으면 총 전압이 셀 수에 비례해 커짐(총 전압 = n: Explain that stacking cells (layers) in series makes the total voltage grow in proportion to the number of cells (total voltage = n × voltage per cell).
Grasp that the voltage per cell varies with the metal pair (electrode potential difference).
볼타 전지가 정전기와 달리 '지속적인' 전류를 공급하는 최초의 화학 전원: Know that the voltaic pile is the first chemical power source to supply 'continuous' current, unlike static electricity.
볼타 전지(볼타 파일, Voltaic Pile)는 서로 다른 두 금속(예: The voltaic pile (Voltaic Pile) takes as its basic unit a cell in which a cloth soaked in saltwater (an electrolyte) is sandwiched between two different metals (e.g., zinc Zn and copper Cu). Because of the electrode potential difference of the two metals, one cell has a constant electromotive force. If you stack these cells in many layers and connect them in series, the voltage of each cell adds up, producing a large voltage that can drive a continuous current between the top and bottom end electrodes.
예를 들어 아연–구리 셀의 셀당 전압을 약 1.1 V라 하면, 같은 셀을: For example, if the voltage per cell of a zinc–copper cell is about 1.1 V, stacking 10 layers of the same cell gives a total voltage of about 11 V. If the metal pair changes, the electrode potential difference changes, so the voltage per cell changes too.
전압계: 총 전압 = n × 셀당전압: Voltmeter: total voltage = n × voltage per cell
흔한 오개념: \"전기는 마찰로 모은 정전기처럼 한순간만 흐른다\"고 생: Common misconception: it is easy to think "electricity flows only for an instant, like static electricity gathered by friction." The decisive difference is that the voltaic pile continuously supplies charge through a chemical reaction, so a continuous current flows as long as the circuit is connected. Also, it is not that "electricity is produced just by touching two metals" — there must be an electrolyte (a cloth soaked in saltwater) between them for the cell to work.

2. 셀 수를 2배로 늘리면 총 전압은 어떻게 되는가?: 2. If you double the number of cells, what happens to the total voltage?
이탈리아의 물리학자로 파비아 대학 교수를 지냈다. 동료 갈바니가 개구리: An Italian physicist who served as a professor at the University of Pavia. Against his colleague Galvani, who interpreted the twitching of a frog's leg as 'animal electricity,' he held that electricity arises from the contact of two metals and an electrolyte. At the end of this debate, in 1800, he invented the 'voltaic pile,' which produces continuous current by alternately stacking different metal disks and cloths soaked in saltwater. The unit of voltage, the volt (V), is named after him.
1780년경 — 갈바니가 개구리 다리 경련 실험에서 '동물 전기'를 주장: c. 1780 — Galvani claims 'animal electricity' from experiments on the twitching of frog legs.
1790년대 — 볼타가 금속 접촉설을 내세워 갈바니와 학문적으로 대립: 1790s — Volta puts forward the metal-contact theory and clashes academically with Galvani.
1800년 — 볼타가 볼타 파일(전지)을 발명, 최초의 지속적 전류원을: 1800 — Volta invents the voltaic pile (battery), presenting the first source of continuous current.
1800년 — 니콜슨·칼라일이 볼타 전지로 물을 전기분해해 화학에 응용: 1800 — Nicholson and Carlisle electrolyze water with the voltaic pile, applying it to chemistry.
1807년~ — 데이비가 강력한 전지로 나트륨·칼륨 등 새 원소를 분리: 1807 onward — Davy uses powerful batteries to isolate new elements such as sodium and potassium.
1820년 — 외르스테드가 전류의 자기 작용을 발견, 전자기학의 문을 엶: 1820 — Ørsted discovers the magnetic action of a current, opening the door to electromagnetism.
과학사적 의의: 볼타 전지는 인류 최초로 지속적인 전류를 공급한 장치로,: Significance in the history of science: the voltaic pile is the first device to supply continuous current to humanity, ending the age of static electricity and opening the 'age of current.' Once a stable power source existed, research in electrolysis, electrochemistry, and the electromagnetism that followed through Ørsted, Ampère, and Faraday developed explosively. It is the direct ancestor of every battery today, and its name remains in the unit of voltage, the volt (V).
💡 Observation point: Bright and dark bands (interference fringes) appear alternately on the screen. Increasing the slit spacing d makes the fringes denser (the spacing narrows), and increasing the wavelength λ (toward red) makes the fringes wider. Increasing the distance L spreads the fringes out. The color of light corresponds to wavelength.
Understand that light passing through two slits overlaps and produces constructive and destructive interference.
무늬 간격 공식 Δy = λ·L / d 의 각 변수가 간섭무늬에 주는 영: Explain how each variable in the fringe-spacing formula Δy = λ·L / d affects the interference fringes.
세기 분포 I(x) ∝ cos²(π·d·x / (λ·L)) 가 밝고 어두: Know that the intensity distribution I(x) ∝ cos²(π·d·x / (λ·L)) creates the bright and dark bands.
Grasp that this experiment is evidence showing the wave nature of light.
단색광이 매우 가까운 두 슬릿을 지나면, 각 슬릿이 새로운 파원이 되어: When monochromatic light passes through two very close slits, each slit becomes a new source of waves and the light spreads out (diffraction). The two beams meet at a point on the screen, and depending on the difference in the two path lengths (path difference), if the phases match it becomes bright (constructive interference), and if they are opposite it becomes dark (destructive interference). As a result, an interference pattern of regularly repeating bright and dark bands appears.
경로차가 파장의 정수배일 때 보강간섭이 일어난다: d·sinθ = m·λ: Constructive interference occurs when the path difference is an integer multiple of the wavelength: d·sinθ = m·λ (m = 0, ±1, ±2 …). When the screen is far enough (L ≫ d), the spacing between adjacent bright bands becomes uniform.
흔한 오개념: \"슬릿이 두 개니까 스크린에 밝은 띠가 딱 두 줄 생긴다: Common misconception: it is easy to think "since there are two slits, there will be exactly two bright bands on the screen." In reality, because light is a wave, the light from the two slits interferes and produces many bright and dark bands. If light were a simple particle, only two bright dots in the shape of the slits should be seen. The very existence of the fringes is evidence of the wave nature.
1. 슬릿 간격 d를 넓히면 무늬 간격 Δy는 어떻게 되는가?: 1. If you widen the slit spacing d, what happens to the fringe spacing Δy?
2. 같은 장치에서 파란빛(짧은 λ) 대신 빨간빛(긴 λ)을 쓰면 무늬: 2. In the same apparatus, if you use red light (long λ) instead of blue light (short λ), what happens to the fringe spacing Δy?
영국의 의사·물리학자·언어학자로, 13세에 여러 고대어를 익힌 신동이었다: An English physician, physicist, and linguist, a prodigy who learned several ancient languages by age 13. He contributed to medicine and physiological optics (accommodation of the eye, the three-color theory of color vision), and also left his name in "Young's modulus" related to elasticity. He also contributed to the development of Egyptology through his work deciphering the Rosetta Stone. From 1801 to 1804, he demonstrated the interference of light by experiment, directly challenging Newton's then-dominant particle theory of light.
1690년 — 하위헌스가 빛의 파동설을 제안 (뉴턴의 입자설과 대립): 1690 — Huygens proposes the wave theory of light (in opposition to Newton's particle theory).
1704년 — 뉴턴의 「광학(Opticks)」 출간, 입자설이 약 1세기: 1704 — Newton's "Opticks" is published, with the particle theory established as the mainstream for about a century.
1801년 — 토머스 영이 간섭 원리를 발표하고 이중 슬릿 간섭무늬를 제: 1801 — Thomas Young announces the principle of interference and presents the double-slit interference fringes.
1818년 — 프레넬이 회절 이론을 수학적으로 정교화하여 파동설을 굳힘: 1818 — Fresnel mathematically refines diffraction theory, solidifying the wave theory.
1865년 — 맥스웰이 빛을 전자기파로 설명, 파동성이 이론적으로 확립: 1865 — Maxwell explains light as an electromagnetic wave, establishing the wave nature theoretically.
1909년~ — 단일 광자·전자로도 간섭무늬가 나타남이 확인되어 양자역학: 1909 onward — It is confirmed that interference fringes appear even with single photons or electrons, making it a core experiment of quantum mechanics.
과학사적 의의: 이중 슬릿 실험은 빛이 파동임을 보여준 결정적 증거로,: Significance in the history of science: the double-slit experiment was decisive evidence showing that light is a wave, shaking Newton's particle theory that had been the accepted view for nearly a century. Later it was revealed that particles such as electrons and atoms also produce the same interference fringes, and this experiment became a symbol of quantum mechanics, demonstrating wave–particle duality. Richard Feynman described it as "the only phenomenon that contains all the mystery of quantum mechanics."
진동면 회전 주기:: Rotation period of the swing plane:
💡 관찰 포인트: 진자는 같은 직선을 따라 왕복하지만, 그 진동면(swi: 💡 Observation point: The pendulum swings back and forth along the same straight line, but its swing plane slowly rotates clockwise (in the Northern Hemisphere) due to Earth's rotation. If you lower the latitude to 0° (the equator), the swing plane does not rotate at all, and if you raise it to 90° (the pole), it makes exactly one turn in 24 hours. Watch the swing plane rotate and knock down the pins on the outer circle one by one.
푸코 진자의 진동면이 회전하는 이유가 진자가 아닌 지구의 자전임을 이해한: Understand that the reason the swing plane of a Foucault pendulum rotates is not the pendulum but the rotation of Earth.
Know that the angular speed of the swing plane's rotation is proportional to the sine (sin) of the latitude.
회전 주기 T = 24h / sin(위도) 와 시간당 회전각 = 15°: Calculate the rotation period T = 24h / sin(latitude) and the rotation angle per hour = 15° × sin(latitude).
Explain how the swing-plane behavior differs at the equator (0°) and at the pole (90°).
Recognize the difference in perspective between an inertial frame and the rotating Earth (a non-inertial frame).
매단 진자는 한 번 흔들리기 시작하면 외부에서 옆으로 미는 힘이 없는 한: Once a suspended pendulum begins to swing, it tends to maintain the same swing plane unless an external sideways force acts on it (conservation of angular momentum). But because the Earth we stand on rotates beneath it, to an observer fixed to the ground the swing plane appears to slowly rotate on its own.
지구 자전의 효과는 위도에 따라 달라진다. 극(90°)에서는 지면이 진자: The effect of Earth's rotation varies with latitude. At the pole (90°), the ground turns once a day around the pendulum's vertical axis just as it is, so the swing plane also makes one turn in 24 hours. At the equator (0°), the rotational component about the pendulum axis is 0, so the swing plane does not rotate at all. At a general latitude φ, only the component sin φ acts.
진동면 회전 속도는 적도에서 0, 극에서 최대(24시간에 한 바퀴)이며: The swing plane's rotation speed is 0 at the equator and maximal at the pole (one turn in 24 hours), proportional to sin(latitude).
흔한 오개념: \"진자가 스스로 옆으로 도는 힘을 받는다\"고 생각하기: Common misconception: it is easy to think "the pendulum receives a force that turns it sideways on its own." In reality the pendulum's swing plane is (ideally) nearly fixed relative to the universe, and what rotates is the Earth we stand on. Also, at the equator a Foucault pendulum does not rotate — not because the pendulum has stopped, but because at that location there is no rotational component about the pendulum axis (sin 0° = 0).

과학자: 레옹 푸코 (Jean Bernard Léon Foucault,: Scientist: Léon Foucault (Jean Bernard Léon Foucault, 1819–1868)
A French physicist who originally studied medicine but turned to experimental physics. He precisely measured the speed of light using a rotating-mirror method, coined the name gyroscope, and proved Earth's rotation with its principle as well. In 1851 he succeeded in an experiment that showed Earth's rotation directly to the eye on the ground, with no telescope or astronomical observation, by suspending a huge pendulum.
1543년 — 코페르니쿠스, 지동설(태양 중심설) 제기. 그러나 자전의: 1543 — Copernicus proposes the heliocentric model (Sun-centered theory). But direct evidence of rotation was lacking.
1851년 2월 — 푸코, 파리 자택 지하실에서 2m 진자로 진동면 회전: February 1851 — Foucault first observes the swing-plane rotation with a 2 m pendulum in the basement of his home in Paris.
1851년 3월 — 파리 팡테옹(Panthéon)에 길이 67m, 추 2: March 1851 — He installs a large pendulum 67 m long with a 28 kg bob at the Panthéon in Paris for a public demonstration.
1852년 — 푸코, 자이로스코프를 발명하여 또 다른 방식으로 지구 자전: 1852 — Foucault invents the gyroscope, proving Earth's rotation by yet another method.
이후 — 세계 각지 과학관·대학에 푸코 진자가 설치되어 지구 자전의 상징: Afterward — Foucault pendulums are installed in science museums and universities around the world, becoming a symbol of Earth's rotation.
과학사적 의의: 코페르니쿠스 이후 300년 동안 지구 자전은 천문 관측으: Significance in the history of science: for 300 years after Copernicus, Earth's rotation could only be inferred from astronomical observation and was hard to show directly by a ground experiment. The Foucault pendulum let anyone see with their own eyes the swing plane slowly rotating, proving inside a laboratory that Earth rotates. It is a leading example of visualizing an effect that appears in a rotating reference frame (the Coriolis effect), and it broadened the understanding of non-inertial frames in classical mechanics.

The mechanical work lost by the weight does not disappear but is entirely converted into the water's heat (internal energy). This is conservation of energy (the first law of thermodynamics). Reducing the amount of water makes the temperature rise more for the same work.
Understand that mechanical work is converted into heat (the heat–work equivalence).

높이 h에서 질량 m의 추가 떨어질 때 중력이 한 역학적 일은 W = m: When a weight of mass m falls from height h, the mechanical work done by gravity is W = m·g·h. This weight is connected by a pulley to a rotating paddle in the water, so as it falls the paddle churns the water. The viscous friction of the water converts all of the weight's mechanical work into heat.
물이 흡수한 열 Q는 일 W와 같고(에너지 보존), 이때 물의 온도는 Δ: The heat Q absorbed by the water equals the work W (conservation of energy), and the water's temperature rises by ΔT = Q / (m_water·c). Here c is the specific heat of water, 4186 J/(kg·K). With this experiment, Joule precisely measured "the amount of work needed to produce a unit of heat," that is, the mechanical equivalent of heat (about 4.186 J/cal).
추의 역학적 일이 날개의 마찰을 거쳐 물의 열로 변환된다. 에너지는 형태: The weight's mechanical work is converted into the water's heat via the paddle's friction. Energy only changes form and is conserved.
흔한 오개념: \"물을 휘젓는 일은 그냥 없어진다\" 또는 \"열은 물체: Common misconception: it is easy to think "the work of churning the water simply disappears," or "heat is an invisible fluid (caloric) contained in objects." In reality the mechanical work does not disappear but is converted entirely into the disordered motion of molecules — that is, heat (internal energy). Joule's experiment proved that heat is not a separate substance but a form of energy, toppling the caloric theory.
떨어지는 추가 날개를 돌리며 한 역학적 일은 결국 어디로 가는가?: Where does the mechanical work done by the falling weight turning the paddle ultimately go?

다시 추의 위치에너지로 돌아간다: It returns to the weight's potential energy

물의 양과 무관하다: It is independent of the amount of water
과학자: 제임스 프레스콧 줄 (James Prescott Joule, 1: Scientist: James Prescott Joule (James Prescott Joule, 1818–1889)
영국 맨체스터의 양조장 집안에서 태어난 물리학자다. 정규 대학 교육 대신: A physicist born into a brewing family in Manchester, England. Instead of a formal university education he was taught by the chemist John Dalton, and he continued his research through self-study and precise experiments while running the family business. He excelled at quantitative experiments linking electricity, mechanics, and heat, and personally handled extremely precise thermometers that could catch tiny temperature changes.
1843년부터 추-날개 장치로 역학적 일이 만드는 열을 반복 측정해 역학: From 1843 he repeatedly measured the heat produced by mechanical work with a weight-and-paddle apparatus, obtaining the mechanical equivalent of heat. The unit of energy, the joule (J), comes from his name.
18세기 — 라부아지에 등의 칼로릭(열소)설이 열을 보존되는 유체로 설명: 18th century — The caloric theory of Lavoisier and others, explaining heat as a conserved fluid, becomes the accepted view.
1798년 — 럼퍼드가 대포 천공 실험에서 마찰이 끝없이 열을 만든다고: 1798 — Rumford reports that in a cannon-boring experiment, friction produces heat endlessly (casting doubt on the caloric theory).
1843년 — 줄, 추-날개(paddle wheel) 실험으로 열-일 등: 1843 — Joule begins measuring the heat–work equivalence with the weight-and-paddle (paddle wheel) experiment.
1845~1850년 — 정밀도를 높여 역학적 열당량 약 4.16 J/ca: 1845–1850 — Increasing the precision, he announces a mechanical equivalent of heat of about 4.16 J/cal (close to the modern value of 4.186 J/cal).
1847년 — 헬름홀츠가 에너지 보존 원리를 정식화, 줄의 결과가 핵심: 1847 — Helmholtz formulates the principle of conservation of energy, with Joule's result used as key evidence.
1850년대 — 켈빈·클라우지우스가 열역학 제1·제2법칙을 체계화: 1850s — Kelvin and Clausius systematize the first and second laws of thermodynamics.
과학사적 의의: 줄의 실험은 \"열은 보존되는 물질(칼로릭)\"이라는 오: Significance in the history of science: Joule's experiment toppled the old notion that "heat is a conserved substance (caloric)" and quantitatively proved that heat is a form of energy. The fact that mechanical work and heat are interconvertible in an exact ratio became the experimental foundation of the law of conservation of energy (the first law of thermodynamics) and thereafter supported the entire field of thermodynamics. The international unit of energy, the joule (J), being named after him honors this contribution.
💡 관찰 포인트: 고온 열원에서 들어온 열 Qh 중 일부만 일 W로 바뀌: 💡 Observation point: Of the heat Qh coming in from the hot reservoir, only part is converted into work W, and the rest Qc is dumped into the cold reservoir. Lowering Tc or raising Th thickens the work (W) arrow and increases the efficiency. But since Tc = 0 K is impossible, the efficiency never reaches 100%. Also, Tc is always kept lower than Th.
열기관이 고온·저온 두 열원 사이에서 작동하며 열의 일부만 일로 바꾼다는: Understand that a heat engine operates between two reservoirs, hot and cold, and converts only part of the heat into work.
Know that the Carnot efficiency η = 1 − Tc/Th is determined by absolute temperatures (K).
어떤 열기관도 같은 두 온도에서 카르노 효율을 넘을 수 없음(열역학 제2: Grasp that no heat engine can exceed the Carnot efficiency at the same two temperatures (the second law of thermodynamics).
효율을 높이는 방법(Th ↑, Tc ↓)과 100%가 불가능한 이유를 설: Explain how to raise the efficiency (Th ↑, Tc ↓) and why 100% is impossible.
카르노 기관은 두 등온 과정과 두 단열 과정으로 이루어진 가역 순환(카르: The Carnot engine is an ideal heat engine that operates on a reversible cycle (the Carnot cycle) consisting of two isothermal processes and two adiabatic processes. It absorbs heat Qh from the hot reservoir (Th), converts part of it into work W, and expels the remaining heat Qc to the cold reservoir (Tc). By conservation of energy, W = Qh − Qc.
카르노는 가역 기관에서 흡수·방출 열의 비가 온도의 비와 같음(Qc/Qh: Carnot showed that in a reversible engine the ratio of absorbed to expelled heat equals the ratio of temperatures (Qc/Qh = Tc/Th), and therefore the efficiency is η = W/Qh = 1 − Qc/Qh = 1 − Tc/Th. This is the theoretical maximum efficiency determined by the two temperatures alone, which no real engine can exceed.
흔한 오개념: \"기관을 정교하게 만들면 열을 100% 일로 바꿀 수 있: Common misconception: it is easy to think "if you build the engine precisely, you can convert heat 100% into work." However, for a heat engine to do work it must have a cold reservoir to dump heat into, and for the efficiency to be 100% the cold reservoir would have to be at Tc = 0 K (absolute zero), which cannot be reached. Even an ideal engine without friction or heat loss has its efficiency limited to 1 − Tc/Th (the second law of thermodynamics).

2. 효율을 100%로 만들 수 없는 이유로 옳은 것은?: 2. Which is the correct reason the efficiency cannot be made 100%?

= 0 K(절대영도)에 도달할 수 없어서: Because Tc = 0 K (absolute zero) cannot be reached
고온 열원의 열이 무한하지 않아서: Because the heat of the hot reservoir is not infinite
과학자: 사디 카르노 (Nicolas Léonard Sadi Carnot: Scientist: Sadi Carnot (Nicolas Léonard Sadi Carnot, 1796–1832)
프랑스의 군인이자 물리학자·공학자로 \"열역학의 아버지\"라 불린다. 1: A French soldier, physicist, and engineer called "the father of thermodynamics." In 1824, through a single book, "Reflections on the Motive Power of Fire (Réflexions sur la puissance motrice du feu)," he revealed that the maximum efficiency of a heat engine depends only on the operating temperatures and is independent of the working substance. Even though the caloric theory, viewing heat as a substance ('caloric'), prevailed at the time, his reasoning became the foundation of the second law of thermodynamics that would later be established. He died young of cholera at 36, and his achievements were rediscovered by Clausius and Kelvin.
1769년 — 제임스 와트가 효율을 개선한 증기기관 특허 (산업혁명의 동: 1769 — James Watt patents a steam engine with improved efficiency (the driving force of the Industrial Revolution).
1824년 — 사디 카르노가 이상적 열기관과 최대 효율의 개념을 제시: 1824 — Sadi Carnot presents the concept of the ideal heat engine and maximum efficiency.
1834년 — 클라페롱이 카르노의 아이디어를 P–V 도표와 수식으로 정식: 1834 — Clapeyron formalizes Carnot's ideas with a P–V diagram and equations.
1850년 — 클라우지우스가 열역학 제2법칙을 명확히 진술: 1850 — Clausius clearly states the second law of thermodynamics.
1851년 — 켈빈(윌리엄 톰슨)이 절대온도 척도와 제2법칙을 정립: 1851 — Kelvin (William Thomson) establishes the absolute-temperature scale and the second law.
과학사적 의의: 카르노의 분석은 열기관의 효율에 절대적 상한이 존재함을: Significance in the history of science: Carnot's analysis first showed that an absolute upper limit exists on the efficiency of a heat engine, and this led to the second law of thermodynamics — "heat does not flow spontaneously from a cold place to a hot place" — and to the concept of entropy. The insight that efficiency is determined not by the working substance but by the two temperatures alone became the physical basis of the absolute-temperature (Kelvin) scale, and remains today the theoretical reference point in the design of power plants, refrigerators, and engines.

유도 전류의 방향이 변화를 방해하는 쪽으로 흐른다는 렌츠 법칙을 이해한다: Understand Lenz's law, that the induced current flows in the direction that opposes the change.

코일을 관통하는 자기 선속(자속) Φ가 시간에 따라 변하면, 코일 양 끝: When the magnetic flux Φ passing through a coil changes over time, a voltage (electromotive force, EMF) is induced across the ends of the coil, and a current flows in the circuit. The key is the change of flux. If the magnet is at rest relative to the coil, no matter how strong the magnet, the flux does not change, so the induced current is 0.
자속의 변화가 빠를수록(자석을 빨리 움직일수록), 코일의 감은 수 N이: The faster the flux changes (the faster you move the magnet), the more coil turns N, and the stronger the magnet, the greater the induced EMF. The direction of the induced current is set to oppose the change of flux (Lenz's law). This is why the current direction is opposite when the magnet enters and when it exits.
자석이 코일에 다가가면 코일을 통과하는 자속 Φ가 증가하고, 그 변화에: As the magnet approaches the coil, the flux Φ through the coil increases, and an EMF proportional to that change is induced.
흔한 오개념: \"강한 자석을 코일 속에 넣어두기만 해도 전류가 계속 흐: Common misconception: it is easy to think "just keeping a strong magnet inside the coil keeps a current flowing." But if the magnet is at rest inside the coil, the flux does not change, so the induced current is 0. What produces the current is not the magnet's strength itself but the change of flux (the motion).

영국의 물리학자·화학자로, 정규 교육을 거의 받지 못하고 제본소 견습공으: An English physicist and chemist who received almost no formal education and worked as a bookbinding apprentice before becoming a scientist through self-study. Starting as Humphry Davy's assistant, he researched his whole life at the Royal Institution. Though weak in mathematics, with outstanding experimental intuition he discovered electromagnetic induction, the laws of electrolysis, the Faraday effect, and more.
그는 자기와 전기를 잇는 보이지 않는 장(field) 개념을 도입했고,: He introduced the concept of an invisible field connecting magnetism and electricity, and this became the foundation on which Maxwell later completed electromagnetism mathematically. 1820년 — 외르스테드, 전류가 자침을 움직임을 발견 (전기→자기): 1820 — Ørsted discovers that a current moves a magnetic needle (electricity → magnetism).
1820년대 — 앙페르·비오·사바르 등이 전류와 자기장의 관계를 정량화: 1820s — Ampère, Biot, Savart, and others quantify the relationship between current and magnetic field.
1831년 — 패러데이, 코일과 자석 실험으로 전자기 유도 발견 (자기→: 1831 — Faraday discovers electromagnetic induction through coil-and-magnet experiments (magnetism → electricity).

1865년 — 맥스웰, 전자기 방정식으로 패러데이의 장 개념을 수식화: 1865 — Maxwell formulates Faraday's field concept with the electromagnetic equations.
과학사적 의의: 외르스테드가 \"전기로 자기를 만들 수 있다\"는 것을: Significance in the history of science: after Ørsted showed that "magnetism can be made from electricity," Faraday proved the converse, that "electricity can be made from magnetism." This discovery became the principle of the generator that produces electricity in bulk, opening the electrical civilization of the late 19th century. Also, the concept of the 'field' he introduced became the fundamental framework for understanding force in modern physics, leading to Maxwell's electromagnetism and later field theories.

Increasing the frequency f decreases the wavelength λ (c = f·λ is constant). For any electromagnetic wave, the speed in vacuum is always the same, c — only the wavelength changes; the speed of light does not.
변하는 전기장이 자기장을, 변하는 자기장이 전기장을 만들어 서로를 지탱함: Understand that a changing electric field creates a magnetic field and a changing magnetic field creates an electric field, so they sustain each other.

빛도 전자기파이며 진공 속도가 c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀) ≈ 3×10⁸ m: Understand that light is also an electromagnetic wave, with a vacuum speed of c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀) ≈ 3×10⁸ m/s.

맥스웰은 전기와 자기를 네 개의 방정식으로 통합했다. 그중 두 식(패러데: Maxwell unified electricity and magnetism into four equations. Two of them (Faraday's law and the Ampère–Maxwell law) are central: a changing magnetic field creates an electric field, and a changing electric field creates a magnetic field. When one changes the other arises, and as that in turn changes it revives the first. In this way E and B sustain each other and propagate through space on their own — this is an electromagnetic wave.

과학사적 의의: 맥스웰 방정식은 뉴턴 역학에 이은 \"두 번째 위대한 통: Significance in the history of science: Maxwell's equations were the "second great unification" after Newtonian mechanics, binding electricity, magnetism, and light into a single electromagnetic-field theory. The prediction of electromagnetic waves became the foundation of technologies underpinning modern civilization — radio, TV, radar, wireless communication, medical imaging, and more. 맥스웰은 변화하는 전기장이 자기장을, 변화하는 자기장이 다시 전기장을 만: Maxwell theoretically predicted the existence of electromagnetic waves — waves in which a changing electric field creates a magnetic field, a changing magnetic field creates an electric field again, and these two, inducing each other, propagate through space at the speed of light c (1865).
헤르츠는 유도코일과 불꽃 간극으로 된 송신기에서 전하를 빠르게 진동·방전: Hertz generated electromagnetic waves by rapidly oscillating and discharging charge in a transmitter made of an induction coil and a spark gap, and by observing the spark induced in a distant receiver loop (a small gap), he demonstrated the existence of these waves experimentally (1887). Reception is maximal when the resonant frequencies of the transmitter and receiver match, and weakens with greater distance.
송신기의 진동 방전이 전자기파를 만들고, 공진하는 수신 고리의 간극에 불: The transmitter's oscillating discharge creates an electromagnetic wave, and a spark is induced across the gap of the resonating receiver loop.
흔한 오개념: \"수신기와 송신기가 전선으로 연결돼 있어야 신호가 전달된: Common misconception: it is easy to misunderstand that "the receiver and transmitter must be connected by a wire for the signal to be transmitted." The key point of Hertz's experiment is that energy is transmitted across empty space with no connection at all. Also, Hertz saw this merely as a proof of Maxwell's theory and thought it "of no use," but Marconi soon made it practical as wireless telegraphy.
전류는 도선을 통해서만 흐른다: That current flows only through a wire

독일의 물리학자로 헬름홀츠의 제자였다. 카를스루에 공과대학 교수 시절인: A German physicist and a student of Helmholtz. During his time as a professor at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology in 1886–1889, through a series of experiments using an induction coil and a spark gap, he first proved experimentally the existence of the electromagnetic waves predicted by Maxwell. He showed that electromagnetic waves are reflected, refracted, interfere, and are polarized, and propagate at the same speed as light, confirming that light is indeed an electromagnetic wave.
주파수의 SI 단위 헤르츠(Hz)는 그의 이름에서 따왔다. 정작 그는 이: The SI unit of frequency, the hertz (Hz), is named after him. When asked about the practical value of this discovery, he actually answered that it was "of no use whatsoever (Nichts, glaube ich)," yet just a few years later it became the foundation of the wireless-communication revolution. He died young at 36 from a vascular disease.

Experience that a macroscopic state (temperature) is explained by the statistics of countless microstates.
기체 한 통 속에는 약 10²³개의 분자가 있고, 분자 하나하나는 충돌하: A container of gas holds about 10²³ molecules, and each molecule's speed changes ceaselessly as it collides. Tracking individual molecules is impossible, but the distribution of speeds follows a definite statistical law. This is the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution.
속력 v를 가진 분자의 상대적 비율은 f(v) ∝ v²·exp(−m·v²: The relative fraction of molecules with speed v is given by f(v) ∝ v²·exp(−m·v²/(2kT)). The v² in front indicates that the faster the speed, the more directions (the shell in 3D velocity space) correspond to it, and the exponential term behind indicates that the larger the kinetic energy, the rarer such molecules are. These two effects compete, producing a single peak (the most-probable speed).
온도 T는 분자들의 평균 운동에너지의 척도다. 온도를 높이면 지수항이 완: Temperature T is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the molecules. Raising the temperature makes the exponential term gentler, so the fraction of fast molecules increases, the whole distribution spreads to the right, and the peak becomes lower and broader.
볼츠만은 더 나아가, 거시 상태(예: 특정 온도)에 대응하는 미시 상태의: Boltzmann went further, holding that the more microstates W correspond to a macroscopic state (e.g., a particular temperature), the more "disordered" that state is, and that nature heads in that direction. Defining this as entropy is S = k·ln W.
온도가 높아지면 최빈 속도(점선)가 커지고, 봉우리가 낮아지며 분포가 오: As the temperature rises, the most-probable speed (dashed line) increases, the peak lowers, and the distribution spreads out widely to the right.
흔한 오개념: \"같은 온도의 기체에서는 모든 분자가 같은 속도로 움직인: Common misconception: it is easy to misunderstand that "in a gas at a given temperature, all molecules move at the same speed." In reality they are distributed over a wide range, from very slow molecules to very fast ones. Temperature represents not the speed of an individual molecule but the average kinetic energy. Also, entropy is often confused as "entropy = garbage/dirtiness," when it is the logarithm of the number of microscopic arrangements (W) that produce the same macroscopic state.
