기체가 한 일의 양: The amount of work done by the gas
하나의 거시 상태에 대응하는 미시 상태의 수: The number of microstates corresponding to one macroscopic state
분자 1개의 운동에너지: The kinetic energy of a single molecule
오스트리아 빈 출신의 물리학자로, 열과 기체의 거동을 수많은 원자·분자의: A physicist from Vienna, Austria, who established statistical mechanics, explaining the behavior of heat and gases through the statistical motion of a great many atoms and molecules. He generalized Maxwell's speed distribution and presented the formula S = k·ln W, connecting entropy with the number of microstates. This formula is engraved on his tombstone.
당시 원자의 실재를 의심하는 마흐(Mach)·오스트발트(Ostwald): At the time he fiercely debated the energeticists such as Mach and Ostwald, who doubted the reality of atoms, and in deep depression he took his own life in 1906. A few years later, Perrin's Brownian-motion experiment confirmed the reality of atoms, proving that his theory was correct.

1872년 — 볼츠만, H-정리 발표 (분포가 평형으로 향함을 통계적으로: 1872 — Boltzmann announces the H-theorem (statistically explaining that the distribution heads toward equilibrium).
1877년 — 엔트로피와 확률(미시상태 수)의 관계 정립, S = k·l: 1877 — He establishes the relationship between entropy and probability (the number of microstates), the foundation of the idea S = k·ln W.
1900~1906년 — 원자 실재성을 둘러싼 에너지론자들과의 논쟁 격화: 1900–1906 — The debate with the energeticists over the reality of atoms intensifies.
1909년 — 페랭의 브라운 운동 실험으로 원자·분자의 실재 확증: 1909 — Perrin's Brownian-motion experiment confirms the reality of atoms and molecules.
과학사적 의의: 볼츠만은 거시적 열현상(온도·엔트로피)을 원자·분자의 통: Significance in the history of science: by reducing macroscopic thermal phenomena (temperature, entropy) to the statistical motion of atoms and molecules, Boltzmann gave the second law of thermodynamics a microscopic, probabilistic foundation. The insight that "nature heads toward states of higher probability (more microstates)" became the starting point of statistical physics and later led to information entropy and quantum statistics. In an age when atomism was doubted, he explained the world through the statistics of invisible particles — a cornerstone of modern physics.

💡 관찰 포인트: 에테르 바람 속도 v나 팔 길이 L을 키우면 고전(에테: 💡 Observation point: Increasing the aether wind speed v or the arm length L makes the fringe shift predicted by classical (aether) theory grow larger and larger. Yet even when the apparatus is rotated, the fringes at the actual detector barely move (≈ 0). This 'null result'—the mismatch between prediction and observation—is precisely the starting point of a great discovery.
당시 빛이 '에테르(aether)'라는 매질을 통해 전달된다고 믿었던 배: Understand the background belief of the time that light was transmitted through a medium called the 'aether'.
마이컬슨 간섭계가 직교하는 두 팔의 빛 속도 차이를 어떻게 측정하는지 안: Know how the Michelson interferometer measures the difference in light speed between its two perpendicular arms.
에테르 가설이 예측한 무늬 이동 공식 ΔN ≈ (L/λ)·(v/c)² 의: Explain the meaning of the fringe-shift formula ΔN ≈ (L/λ)·(v/c)² predicted by the aether hypothesis.
실제 관측이 ≈ 0(귀무 결과)이었음과, 그것이 광속 불변·특수상대성으로: Grasp that the actual observation was ≈ 0 (null result), and that this led to the constancy of the speed of light and special relativity.
19세기 물리학자들은 빛이 파동이므로 그것을 전달하는 매질 '에테르'가: Nineteenth-century physicists believed that since light is a wave, a medium called the 'aether' that transmits it filled the universe. If the Earth orbits through the aether at about 30 km per second, an 'aether wind' would blow past the Earth, and the speed of light should differ depending on the direction of travel.
마이컬슨 간섭계는 광원에서 나온 빛을 반투명 거울(빔스플리터)로 둘로 갈: The Michelson interferometer splits light from a source into two with a half-silvered mirror (beam splitter), sends the two beams down two perpendicular arms, reflects them off mirrors at the end of each arm, and recombines them. If there is a difference in the travel time along the two paths, an interference fringe pattern appears when they recombine. If the apparatus is rotated 90° to swap the roles of the two arms, the fringes should shift if the aether exists.
하지만 미켈슨과 몰리가 아무리 정밀하게 측정하고 장치를 회전시켜도 무늬: But no matter how precisely Michelson and Morley measured or rotated the apparatus, the fringe shift was less than 1/40 of the prediction—essentially zero. No aether wind was detected.
흔한 오개념: \"무늬가 움직이지 않았으니 실험은 실패했다\"고 생각하기: Common misconception: It is easy to think "the fringes didn't move, so the experiment failed." In reality, the very fact that nothing changed (a null result) was the decisive discovery. It meant that the aether does not exist and that the speed of light is constant regardless of the observer's motion, and it ultimately opened the road to Einstein's special theory of relativity.

예측대로 큰 무늬 이동이 관측되었다: A large fringe shift was observed, as predicted
빛이 사라져 무늬가 생기지 않았다: Light disappeared and no fringes formed

에테르는 없으며 빛의 속도는 일정하다(광속 불변): There is no aether and the speed of light is constant (constancy of light speed)

The 'Michelson interferometer' he invented was a precision instrument that captured extremely tiny differences in length through the interference of light. In 1907 he became the first American to win the Nobel Prize in Physics.
몰리는 미국의 화학자로, 정밀 측정과 실험 설계에 뛰어났다. 두 사람은: Morley was an American chemist, outstanding in precise measurement and experimental design. In 1887 in Cleveland, the two conducted their experiment together using a delicate interferometer built on a heavy stone slab floated on mercury so it could be rotated smoothly without vibration.

1865년 — 맥스웰이 빛을 전자기파로 설명, 에테르 가설이 더욱 굳어짐: 1865 — Maxwell explained light as an electromagnetic wave, further entrenching the aether hypothesis
1881년 — 미켈슨이 단독으로 첫 간섭계 실험을 수행(정밀도 부족): 1881 — Michelson performed the first interferometer experiment on his own (lacking precision)

The denser the material and the higher its atomic number (bone, lead), the more X-rays it absorbs, so less light reaches the detector plate and it appears white on the photograph (film). Conversely, places that transmit well, like flesh and air, appear black. Raising the tube voltage (energy) increases transmission so the same material appears darker, and increasing the thickness x increases absorption so it appears whiter.

투과 세기가 두께에 따라 지수적으로 감소함을 식 I = I₀·e−μx 로: Explain that the transmitted intensity decreases exponentially with thickness using the equation I = I₀·e−μx.
Know that the attenuation coefficient μ becomes larger the greater the material's density and atomic number.
Explain why bone and metal appear white, and flesh and air appear black, on an X-ray photograph.
X선은 파장이 매우 짧은 전자기파로, 가시광선과 달리 물질을 꿰뚫고 지나: X-rays are electromagnetic waves of very short wavelength that, unlike visible light, penetrate through matter. But as they pass through, they collide with the atoms of the material and some are absorbed and scattered, reducing the intensity (attenuation). The remaining intensity I starts from the initial intensity I₀ and decreases exponentially as the thickness x increases.
감쇠의 정도를 나타내는 값이 선형 감쇠계수 μ이다. μ는 물질마다 다르며: The value that expresses the degree of attenuation is the linear attenuation coefficient μ. μ differs for each material and is larger for materials of higher density and higher atomic number (Z) (air ≪ flesh < aluminum ≈ bone ≪ lead). Also, the higher the X-ray energy (tube voltage), the smaller μ becomes and the better the transmission. The detector plate (film) turns darker the more X-rays reach it, so behind strongly-absorbing bone and metal fewer X-rays arrive and it stays white (bright), while behind flesh and air it appears black.
흔한 오개념: \"X선 사진에서 뼈가 희게 나오는 건 뼈가 빛(X선)을: Common misconception: It is easy to think "bone appears white on an X-ray because bone lets a lot of light (X-rays) through." The truth is exactly the opposite. Because bone has high density and atomic number, it absorbs many X-rays, so few X-rays reach the detector plate, and that part of the film turns less dark and stays white. In other words, white means "heavily blocked."

In November 1895, while experimenting with a cathode-ray tube (Crookes tube) wrapped in black paper, he accidentally noticed that a nearby fluorescent screen was glowing. He took an image of his wife Anna Bertha's hand, leaving the first medical X-ray photograph showing bones and a ring. Since the cathode ray is drawn toward the (+) plate, we can tell the particles carry negative charge (electrons). When both fields are applied together and tuned so the deflection is zero (straight travel), the electric force equals the magnetic force (qE = qvB), giving the velocity v = E/B, from which e/m is then calculated. Whatever gas is used at the cathode, the same e/m results — evidence that it is a particle common to all atoms.

음극선관은 음극(cathode)에서 튀어나온 입자 빔을 가속 전압 Va로: In a cathode-ray tube, a beam of particles ejected from the cathode is accelerated by the accelerating voltage Va, then passed through a region of parallel deflection plates (electric field E) and a magnetic field B. Finally the beam strikes a fluorescent screen, creating a bright spot of light.
전기장만 걸면 입자는 한쪽으로 휘고, 자기장만 걸면 (로런츠 힘 방향이: With only the electric field applied, the particles bend to one side; with only the magnetic field applied, they bend the other way (because the Lorentz force is in the opposite direction). When the two forces are made equal in magnitude (qE = qvB), the beam travels straight without bending. In this case the velocity is determined as v = E/B (velocity selector). Once the velocity v is known, combining it with the deflection under the electric field alone allows the particle's specific charge e/m to be found.
The beam from the cathode passes through the accelerating and deflecting regions and makes a spot of light on the fluorescent screen.

This opened the age of particle physics and atomic-structure research, and became the starting point of modern physics that soon led to the atomic nucleus and quantum mechanics.

에너지 양자화(E = hf)가 자외선 파탄을 해결하며 양자역학을 열었음을: Grasp that energy quantization (E = hf) resolved the ultraviolet catastrophe and opened quantum mechanics.
모든 빛을 흡수하는 이상적인 물체(흑체)는 자기 온도에 따라 빛을 방출한: An ideal object that absorbs all light (a blackbody) emits light according to its own temperature. Its intensity differs by wavelength, and the entire distribution is determined solely by the temperature T. As the temperature rises, the total radiation grows sharply (Stefan–Boltzmann, ∝T⁴), and the wavelength λmax at which it glows brightest becomes shorter (Wien's displacement law).
19세기 말 고전 물리(레일리–진스 법칙)는 짧은 파장에서 세기가 1/λ: At the end of the 19th century, classical physics (the Rayleigh–Jeans law) predicted that the intensity would grow infinitely as 1/λ⁴ at short wavelengths — the ultraviolet catastrophe, completely at odds with actual observation. In 1900 Planck assumed that oscillators exchange energy not continuously but only in chunks (quanta) of E = hf, and thereby reproduced the actual spectrum exactly. This assumption became the starting point of the quantum concept.
Common misconception: It is easy to think "a hotter object glows redder." In reality it is the opposite — as the temperature rises the peak shifts to shorter (blue) wavelengths, so the color changes from red → orange → white → blue. There is also the misunderstanding that "quantization applies only to light," but what Planck first quantized was not light itself but the energy of the oscillators in the blackbody walls.

독일의 이론물리학자로 열역학과 복사 이론을 연구했다. 1900년 흑체복사: A German theoretical physicist who studied thermodynamics and radiation theory. In 1900, to accurately explain the blackbody-radiation spectrum, he introduced the 'quantum hypothesis' that energy is exchanged only in integer multiples of hf, and the proportionality constant that appeared here is precisely Planck's constant h (6.626×10⁻³⁴ J·s). He himself long hesitated to accept it, calling it "a mathematical trick born of desperation," but this hypothesis became the starting point of modern quantum mechanics. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1918.

It then led to Einstein's light quanta, Bohr's atomic model, and de Broglie's matter waves, changing the paradigm of 20th-century physics.
💡 관찰 포인트: 먼저 진동수 f를 문턱 진동수 f₀보다 낮게 둔 채로: 💡 Observation point: First, keep the frequency f below the threshold frequency f₀ and turn the light intensity up to maximum. No matter how bright you make it, not a single electron comes out. Conversely, if you raise f to f₀ or above, electrons are emitted immediately even when the intensity is 1. This phenomenon—no electrons emitted at low frequency no matter how bright the light—cannot be explained by classical wave theory.

Know the relationship between the threshold frequency f₀ and the work function W = h·f₀.
광전 방정식 KEₘₐₓ = h·f − W 를 적용해 방출 전자의 운동에너: Apply the photoelectric equation KEₘₐₓ = h·f − W to calculate the kinetic energy of emitted electrons.

금속 표면에 빛을 비추면 전자(광전자)가 튀어나온다. 고전 파동론은 \": When light shines on a metal surface, electrons (photoelectrons) are ejected. Classical wave theory predicted that "if you shine bright (intense) light for a long time, energy will accumulate and electrons will come out," but the actual experiment was entirely different.
아인슈타인은 빛이 진동수 f에 비례하는 에너지 덩어리(광자, photon: Einstein regarded light as consisting of energy chunks (photons) E = h·f proportional to the frequency f. A single electron absorbs a single photon whole. The minimum energy needed to tear an electron out of the metal is the work function W, and expressing this as a frequency gives the threshold frequency f₀ = W/h.
광자 에너지가 일함수보다 작으면(f < f₀) 전자는 떨어져 나오지 못한: If the photon energy is less than the work function (f < f₀), the electron cannot be knocked loose. Increasing the intensity only increases the 'number' of photons; since the energy of a single photon (hf) stays the same, electrons still do not come out. Emission occurs only when f ≥ f₀, and the leftover energy becomes the electron's maximum kinetic energy.
f < f₀ 에서는 KEₘₐₓ = 0(방출 없음). f₀ 부터 기울기 h: For f < f₀, KEₘₐₓ = 0 (no emission). From f₀ onward it increases along a straight line of slope h (Planck's constant).
흔한 오개념: \"빛을 더 밝게(세게) 비추면 결국 전자가 나올 것\"이: Common misconception: It is easy to think "if you shine brighter (more intense) light, electrons will eventually come out." But the energy of a single photon depends only on the frequency, so if the frequency is below the threshold, no electrons come out no matter how bright the light. Intensity only increases the 'number' of photons; it cannot increase the energy of a single photon. It is also a common mistake to think "brighter light makes electrons faster," but the electron's speed (KEₘₐₓ) is determined by the frequency.
문턱 진동수보다 낮은 빛의 '세기'를 아무리 키우면 전자는 어떻게 될까?: No matter how much you increase the 'intensity' of light below the threshold frequency, what happens to the electrons?
세기가 커지면 결국 방출된다: As the intensity increases, they are eventually emitted

전자의 최대 운동에너지가 두 배가 된다: The maximum kinetic energy of the electrons is doubled
방출되는 전자의 개수(전류)가 늘어난다: The number of emitted electrons (the current) increases
독일 출신의 이론물리학자로, 1905년 한 해에 광전 효과·브라운 운동·: A German-born theoretical physicist who, in the single year of 1905, published papers on the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity, and the equivalence of mass and energy (E=mc²) one after another, so that this year is called the "Miracle Year (Annus Mirabilis)."
그는 막스 플랑크가 흑체 복사를 설명하려 도입한 에너지 양자(量子) 개념: He extended the concept of the energy quantum, which Max Planck had introduced to explain blackbody radiation, to light itself, proposing that light consists of photons carrying energy E = h·f. With this light-quantum hypothesis he quantitatively explained the photoelectric effect, and it was precisely this achievement that earned him the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics (not the theory of relativity).

An electron from the cathode is accelerated by the accelerating voltage V and gains kinetic energy eV. Along the way it collides with mercury atoms, but if the electron's energy is less than the excitation energy (about 4.9 eV for mercury), it undergoes only elastic collisions in which it loses almost no energy.
전자의 에너지가 4.9 eV에 이르면, 수은 원자가 그 에너지를 통째로: When the electron's energy reaches 4.9 eV, an inelastic collision occurs in which the mercury atom absorbs all of that energy and becomes excited. The electron, having lost its energy, cannot overcome the small retarding voltage in front of the collector (anode), so the collected current drops sharply.
전압을 더 올리면 전자는 충돌 후 다시 가속되어 두 번째로 4.9 eV에: As the voltage is raised further, the electron is re-accelerated after the collision, reaches 4.9 eV a second time, and causes another inelastic collision. Thus the current traces a sawtooth curve that dips repeatedly at intervals of 4.9 V (4.9, 9.8, 14.7 …). If the atom could absorb arbitrary amounts of energy, such regular dips would not appear.

자기 모멘트 μ를 가진 입자가 불균일 자기장(기울기 ∂Bz/∂z)을 지나: When a particle with magnetic moment μ passes through a non-uniform magnetic field (gradient ∂Bz/∂z), it experiences a net force Fz = μz·(∂Bz/∂z) equal to the gradient of the magnetic potential energy U = −μ·B, and the beam bends. The direction and magnitude of the deflection depend on the z-component μz of the magnetic moment.
고전적으로 자기 모멘트는 어떤 방향이든 가질 수 있으므로 μz는 연속적인: Classically the magnetic moment can point in any direction, so μz should take continuous values and a continuous band spread out vertically should appear on the screen. But the actual silver-atom beam split into exactly two points. That is, μz (and hence the spin angular momentum Sz) can take only the two values +ħ/2 and −ħ/2. This is called space quantization.
같은 빔이라도 고전은 연속 띠(회색)를, 양자(실제)는 위·아래 두 점(: For the same beam, the classical case produces a continuous band (gray), while the quantum (actual) case produces only two points, upper and lower (blue and red).
흔한 오개념: \"두 점은 자석이 N극·S극 두 개라서 생긴 것\"이라: Common misconception: It is easy to misunderstand that "the two points arise because a magnet has two poles, N and S." What actually produces the splitting is not the fact that there are two poles but that the magnetic field is spatially non-uniform (if it were uniform, the atom would feel only a torque and zero net force, so the beam would not bend). It is also easy to think "using a stronger magnet produces more points," but increasing the gradient always keeps the number of points at two and only widens the gap. That the number of points is fixed at two is the essence of quantization.
은 원자 빔이 불균일 자기장에서 정확히 위/아래 두 갈래로만 갈라지는 것: The silver-atom beam splitting into exactly two branches, up and down, in a non-uniform magnetic field is evidence of what?
자석에 N극·S극이 있기 때문: Because a magnet has N and S poles
스핀(각운동량)이 양자화되어 두 값만 갖기 때문: Because spin (angular momentum) is quantized and takes only two values
은 원자가 두 종류로 섞여 있기 때문: Because the silver atoms are a mixture of two kinds
고전 물리학(자기 모멘트가 모든 방향을 향할 수 있음)은 스크린에 어떤: What pattern did classical physics (in which the magnetic moment can point in any direction) predict on the screen?
위아래로 연속적으로 퍼진 하나의 띠: A single band spread out continuously up and down
정확히 위·아래 두 개의 점: Exactly two points, up and down
좌우 대칭의 세 개 점: Three points symmetric left and right
오토 슈테른은 독일 출신의 물리학자로 분자선(molecular beam): Otto Stern was a German-born physicist who pioneered the molecular-beam technique. In 1922, together with Walther Gerlach at the University of Frankfurt, he passed a beam of silver atoms through a non-uniform magnetic field and observed the beam split into two branches, directly demonstrating the space quantization of angular momentum for the first time. Stern received the 1943 Nobel Prize in Physics for this molecular-beam method and his measurement of the proton's magnetic moment.
흥미로운 일화로, 검출판에 은 입자가 보이지 않다가 슈테른이 값싼 시가를: As an amusing anecdote, no silver particles were visible on the detector plate until Stern, smoking a cheap cigar, breathed on it — the silver sulfide that formed made the two-streak pattern appear clearly. The sulfur in the cigar effectively acted as a developing agent.
1913년 — 보어의 원자 모형, 각운동량의 양자화 개념 제시: 1913 — Bohr's atomic model introduced the concept of quantized angular momentum
1916년 — 조머펠트, 궤도면의 공간 양자화(space quantiza: 1916 — Sommerfeld theoretically introduced the space quantization of orbital planes
1921년 — 슈테른, 공간 양자화를 직접 검증할 분자선 실험을 제안: 1921 — Stern proposed a molecular-beam experiment to directly verify space quantization
1922년 — 슈테른·게를라흐, 은 원자 빔이 두 갈래로 갈라짐을 관측: 1922 — Stern and Gerlach observed the silver-atom beam splitting into two branches
1925년 — 울런벡·하우트스밋, 전자 \"스핀(spin)\" 개념을 도: 1925 — Uhlenbeck and Goudsmit introduced the concept of electron "spin," explaining the identity of the two branches
1927년 — 수소 원자로 재현, 바닥상태 전자 스핀(½)으로 결과를 재: 1927 — Reproduced with hydrogen atoms, reinterpreting the result in terms of the ground-state electron spin (½)
과학사적 의의: 슈테른-게를라흐 실험은 양자적 관측량이 연속이 아니라 이: Historical significance: The Stern–Gerlach experiment was the first decisive experiment to show, visibly, that a quantum observable takes discrete rather than continuous values. At the time the very concept of "spin" did not exist, but this two-branch pattern soon became direct evidence of electron spin (½), and it laid the foundations of quantum measurement theory — in which measurement "collapses" a quantum state into one of two eigenstates — and, further, of modern quantum technologies such as qubits, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and atomic clocks.
💡 관찰 포인트: 좌측에서 들어온 파동의 일부는 장벽에서 반사되고, 나머: 💡 Observation point: Part of the wave entering from the left is reflected at the barrier, while the rest decays exponentially inside the barrier and then leaks out weakly to the right (tunneling). Increasing the barrier thickness L or the height V₀ makes the transmission probability drop exponentially. In classical mechanics, if E < V₀ the particle can never cross the barrier, but in quantum mechanics it passes through with a nonzero probability.
Understand that barrier crossing, impossible in classical mechanics, is possible in quantum mechanics.
파동함수가 장벽 속에서 지수적으로 감쇠하며 일부가 반대편으로 새어 나감을: Know that the wavefunction decays exponentially inside the barrier and part of it leaks through to the other side.
투과확률 공식 T ≈ exp(−2κL) 에서 두께 L과 높이 V₀의 영향: Explain how thickness L and height V₀ affect the transmission probability in the formula T ≈ exp(−2κL).
Grasp that tunneling is the principle behind alpha decay and the scanning tunneling microscope (STM).
고전적으로 입자가 자기 에너지 E보다 높은 퍼텐셜 장벽(높이 V₀ > E: Classically, when a particle meets a potential barrier higher than its own energy E (height V₀ > E), it can never cross. But in quantum mechanics the particle is described by a wavefunction ψ, and inside the barrier this wavefunction, instead of becoming 0, decays exponentially. If the barrier is thin enough, the wavefunction reaches the other side before it completely vanishes, and there it continues as an oscillating wave again. In other words, the probability of finding the particle beyond the barrier is not zero.
The decay rate inside the barrier is set by κ = √(2m(V₀−E)) / ħ. The larger V₀−E (the energy deficit) and the greater the barrier thickness L, the more the transmission probability shrinks exponentially. This is quantum tunneling — literally "boring through the tunnel."
흔한 오개념: \"입자가 에너지를 잠깐 빌려서 장벽을 '뛰어넘는다'\"고: Common misconception: It is easy to think "the particle borrows energy for a moment and 'leaps over' the barrier." In reality the particle does not go over the top of the barrier; the wavefunction decays inside the barrier yet reaches the other side before becoming 0. It is also a common misunderstanding that "a particle that passes through the barrier loses energy," but the energy E of a tunneled particle does not change. What changes is only the probability of passing through.
1. 장벽 두께 L을 늘리면 양자 터널링 투과확률 T는 어떻게 되는가?: 1. As the barrier thickness L increases, how does the quantum-tunneling transmission probability T change?
두께와 무관하게 일정하다: It stays constant regardless of thickness
2. 입자 에너지 E가 장벽 높이 V₀보다 작을 때(E < V₀), 고전: 2. When the particle energy E is less than the barrier height V₀ (E < V₀), what is the difference between classical and quantum mechanics?
고전은 불가능하지만 양자는 0이 아닌 확률로 통과한다: Classically it is impossible, but quantum-mechanically it passes with a nonzero probability
러시아(현 우크라이나) 태생의 이론물리학자로, 1928년 새로 정립된 양: A theoretical physicist born in Russia (present-day Ukraine) who in 1928 used the newly established quantum mechanics to explain alpha decay. He quantitatively solved, as a probability of tunneling through the barrier, why an alpha particle inside the nucleus is emitted even though it could never classically surmount the high potential barrier created by the nuclear force. He later contributed to Big Bang cosmology's nucleosynthesis (the origin of the elements) and to research on the DNA genetic code, and was also famous as a popular-science author. Around the same time Gurney and Condon independently reached the same conclusion.
1896년 — 베크렐이 방사능 발견, 이후 알파·베타·감마선이 구분됨: 1896 — Becquerel discovered radioactivity, after which alpha, beta, and gamma rays were distinguished
1925~1926년 — 하이젠베르크·슈뢰딩거가 양자역학(행렬역학·파동역학: 1925–1926 — Heisenberg and Schrödinger established quantum mechanics (matrix mechanics and wave mechanics)
1928년 — 가모프(및 거니·콘던)가 양자 터널링으로 알파 붕괴를 설명: 1928 — Gamow (and Gurney and Condon) explained alpha decay by quantum tunneling
1957년 — 에사키가 반도체 터널 다이오드에서 터널링 전류를 실증: 1957 — Esaki demonstrated the tunneling current in a semiconductor tunnel diode
1981년 — 비니히·로러가 주사터널현미경(STM) 발명, 원자를 직접: 1981 — Binnig and Rohrer invented the scanning tunneling microscope (STM), directly imaging atoms
1986년 — STM 공로로 비니히·로러 노벨 물리학상 수상: 1986 — Binnig and Rohrer received the Nobel Prize in Physics for the STM
과학사적 의의: 양자 터널링은 고전역학으로는 절대 불가능한 현상이 양자: Historical significance: Quantum tunneling is a decisive example showing that a phenomenon utterly impossible in classical mechanics is commonplace in the quantum world. It underlies much of modern physics and technology — the half-life of alpha decay, nuclear fusion inside stars (why the Sun shines), semiconductor tunnel diodes, the scanning tunneling microscope (STM) that sees and manipulates atoms, and even the operation of flash memory. It is one of quantum mechanics' triumphs, dramatically proving that an abstract wavefunction accurately predicts real natural phenomena.
💡 관찰 포인트: 막대그래프에서 빨간 점선이 고전 한계 2, 초록 점선이: 💡 Observation point: In the bar chart the red dashed line is the classical limit 2, and the green dashed line is the quantum maximum 2√2 ≈ 2.83. When a bar exceeds 2 and is highlighted, that result cannot be explained by any local hidden-variable theory — it means nature is non-local. Press the "optimal angles" button to confirm that S reaches its maximum 2√2 when a, a', b, b' are staggered by 45° each.
얽힌 두 입자의 측정 상관관계 E(a, b) = −cos(a − b)를: Understand the measurement correlation E(a, b) = −cos(a − b) of two entangled particles.
국소적 숨은 변수(고전) 이론에서는 CHSH 값 |S| ≤ 2 임을 안다: Know that in local hidden-variable (classical) theories the CHSH value satisfies |S| ≤ 2.
양자역학이 특정 각도에서 S = 2√2 ≈ 2.83 으로 부등식을 위배함: Confirm that quantum mechanics violates the inequality at certain angles, reaching S = 2√2 ≈ 2.83.
Grasp that violation of the inequality means the non-locality of nature.
벨의 정리가 \"철학적 논쟁\"을 \"실험으로 판가름할 문제\"로 바꾼: Understand the significance of Bell's theorem in turning a "philosophical debate" into "a question to be settled by experiment."
EPR(아인슈타인·포돌스키·로젠)은 양자역학이 불완전하며, 측정 전에 결: EPR (Einstein, Podolsky, Rosen) argued that quantum mechanics is incomplete and that there must be "hidden variables" that fix the outcomes in advance before measurement (local realism). That is, two distant measurements cannot influence each other (locality), and each particle has definite properties independent of measurement (realism).
벨은 1964년, 이 국소 실재론 가정이 맞다면 측정 상관에 대한 부등식: In 1964 Bell showed that if this assumption of local realism were correct, an inequality on the measurement correlations must hold. Written in CHSH form, the combination S of correlation values measured by two people (Alice and Bob), each at two angles (a, a' and b, b'), cannot classically exceed |S| ≤ 2.
그러나 얽힘 상태의 양자 상관은 E(a, b) = −cos(a − b): But the quantum correlation of an entangled state is E(a, b) = −cos(a − b), and by staggering the four angles by 45° each, S reaches 2√2 ≈ 2.83. Experiments have repeatedly confirmed that quantum mechanics' prediction is correct, so local realism is wrong — nature is non-local.
흔한 오개념: \"얽힘으로 한쪽 측정이 다른 쪽 결과를 즉시 바꾸므로 빛: Common misconception: It is easy to misunderstand that "since entanglement makes one measurement instantly change the other's result, faster-than-light communication is possible." In reality the result seen at each detector is random and by itself carries no information (the no-communication theorem). Non-local correlations exist, but no signal can be sent. Also, violation of Bell's inequality does not mean "quantum mechanics is arbitrarily mysterious"; it quantitatively proves that a specific classical assumption — local realism — is wrong.
1. 측정 결과가 벨 부등식을 위배한다(|S| > 2)는 것은 무엇을 의: 1. What does it mean that the measurement results violate Bell's inequality (|S| > 2)?
국소적 숨은 변수 이론으로는 설명할 수 없다 (양자 얽힘의 비국소성): It cannot be explained by local hidden-variable theories (the non-locality of quantum entanglement)
측정 장치에 오차가 있다는 뜻이다: It means there is an error in the measuring device
2. 양자역학이 도달할 수 있는 CHSH 값 S의 최댓값은?: 2. What is the maximum CHSH value S that quantum mechanics can reach?
북아일랜드 벨파스트 출신의 이론물리학자로, 주로 CERN에서 입자물리학: A theoretical physicist from Belfast, Northern Ireland, who mainly worked at CERN on particle-accelerator design and field theory. His exploration of the foundations of quantum mechanics was closer to a "hobby," but Bell's theorem, published in 1964, is regarded as a landmark achievement of 20th-century physics that moved the EPR debate from metaphysics to experiment. He also left deep insights into the measurement problem and the interpretation of quantum mechanics.
1935년 — 아인슈타인·포돌스키·로젠(EPR)이 양자역학의 불완전성을: 1935 — Einstein, Podolsky, and Rosen (EPR) argued that quantum mechanics is incomplete, criticizing "spooky action at a distance"
1964년 — 존 벨이 국소 숨은 변수 이론이 반드시 만족해야 할 부등식: 1964 — John Bell derived the inequality that any local hidden-variable theory must satisfy (Bell's theorem)
1969년 — 클라우저·혼·시모니·홀트(CHSH)가 실험 가능한 부등식: 1969 — Clauser, Horne, Shimony, and Holt (CHSH) presented an experimentally testable form of the inequality
1972~1982년 — 클라우저, 이어서 아스페가 광자 실험으로 양자 예: 1972–1982 — Clauser, and then Aspect, confirmed the quantum prediction with photon experiments (violation of the inequality)
2015년 — 허점(loophole)을 동시에 막은 결정적 실험들로 비국: 2015 — Decisive experiments that simultaneously closed the loopholes established non-locality
2022년 — 아스페·클라우저·차일링거가 벨 부등식 실험 공로로 노벨 물: 2022 — Aspect, Clauser, and Zeilinger received the Nobel Prize in Physics for their Bell-inequality experiments
과학사적 의의: 벨의 정리는 \"양자역학이 완전한가\"라는 철학적 논쟁을: Historical significance: Bell's theorem turned the philosophical debate "Is quantum mechanics complete?" into a scientific question that could be settled by experiment. As experiments repeatedly violated the inequality, local realism — the idea that everything is predetermined before measurement and cannot affect distant places — was discarded. This established that the non-locality of quantum entanglement is a real property of nature, and it became the foundation of today's quantum cryptography, quantum teleportation, and quantum computing.
c (광속의 비율): c (fraction of the speed of light)
이 흐르는 동안 우주선에서는: elapses, while on the spaceship only
💡 관찰 포인트: 광속 c는 모든 관측자에게 동일합니다. 움직이는 빛 시: 💡 Observation point: The speed of light c is the same for all observers. The light in a moving light-clock must travel a longer diagonal path, but since its speed is the same, one tick takes longer. That is why a moving clock runs slow. Making v small (e.g., 0.1c) makes the two clocks run almost identically, while raising v close to 0.99c makes the difference grow dramatically.
Understand how time dilation follows from the principle of the constancy of the speed of light.
로런츠 인자 γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²)의 의미와 v→c 일 때의: Learn the meaning of the Lorentz factor γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²) and its divergence as v→c.
\"빛 시계\"의 빛 경로가 길어지는 기하로 Δt = γ·Δt₀ 를 유도: Derive Δt = γ·Δt₀ from the geometry in which the light path of a "light clock" lengthens.
일상 속도에서는 효과가 미미하고, 광속 근처에서 극적으로 커짐을 비교한다: Compare how the effect is negligible at everyday speeds and grows dramatically near the speed of light.
특수상대성이론의 두 가정은 (1) 모든 관성계에서 물리 법칙은 동일하고,: The two postulates of special relativity are (1) the laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames, and (2) the speed of light c in vacuum is constant, independent of the motion of the source or the observer.
속도가 빠른 시계를 정지한 관측자가 보면 더 느리게 간다. 움직이는 관측: A fast-moving clock, seen by a stationary observer, runs slower. Between the proper time Δt₀ measured by a moving observer (the time in the frame where the clock is at rest) and the time Δt seen by a stationary observer, the relation Δt = γ·Δt₀ holds. Since γ ≥ 1, the time seen in the rest frame is always longer (= the moving clock runs slow).
빛의 속도가 같으므로 대각선(더 긴) 경로를 도는 움직이는 시계가 한 번: Because the speed of light is the same, the moving clock, whose light travels the longer diagonal path, takes longer for one tick.
흔한 오개념: \"시간 지연은 그냥 시계가 고장 나거나 빨리 움직여서 측: Common misconception: The idea that "time dilation is just the clock breaking or moving fast so the measurement is wrong" is false. Time dilation is not a measurement error but a real effect in which time itself flows differently. It has been confirmed by experiments such as GPS satellite-clock corrections and the extended lifetime of fast-moving muons.
광속에 가깝게 움직이는 우주선의 시계는, 지상에 정지한 관측자가 볼 때: How does the clock of a spaceship moving near the speed of light appear to an observer at rest on the ground?
속도 v가 광속 c에 점점 가까워지면 로런츠 인자 γ는 어떻게 되는가?: As the speed v gets closer and closer to the speed of light c, what happens to the Lorentz factor γ?
독일 태생의 이론물리학자. 1905년 \"기적의 해(Annus Mirab: A German-born theoretical physicist. In 1905, his "miracle year (Annus Mirabilis)," he published a succession of papers on the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity, and mass–energy equivalence (E = mc²). In his special-relativity paper "On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies," he derived time dilation, length contraction, and the relativity of simultaneity from the constancy of the speed of light and the principle of relativity alone.
1915년에는 중력을 시공간의 곡률로 설명하는 일반상대성이론을 완성했고,: In 1915 he completed general relativity, explaining gravity as the curvature of spacetime, and in 1921 he received the Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on the photoelectric effect.
1887년 — 마이컬슨·몰리 실험: 에테르의 흔적을 찾지 못해 광속 불변: 1887 — Michelson–Morley experiment: found no trace of the aether, suggesting the constancy of the speed of light
1892~1904년 — 로런츠, 운동하는 좌표계 사이의 변환(로런츠 변환: 1892–1904 — Lorentz introduced the transformation between moving coordinate frames (the Lorentz transformation) and the factor γ
1905년 — 아인슈타인, 특수상대성이론 발표. 시간 지연 Δt = γ·: 1905 — Einstein published special relativity, deriving time dilation Δt = γ·Δt₀
1908년 — 민코프스키, 시간과 공간을 하나로 묶은 4차원 시공간 개념: 1908 — Minkowski presented the concept of four-dimensional spacetime, binding time and space together
1971년 — 하펠레·키팅 실험: 제트기에 실은 원자시계로 시간 지연 직: 1971 — Hafele–Keating experiment: directly measured time dilation with atomic clocks carried on jet planes
과학사적 의의: 절대적이라 믿었던 시간이 관측자의 운동 상태에 따라 달라: Historical significance: By revealing that time, believed to be absolute, changes with the observer's state of motion, it overturned Newton's concept of absolute spacetime. Time dilation is the starting point leading to the twin paradox, mass–energy equivalence, and general relativity, and today it is a verified physical law actually applied in GPS satellite-clock corrections and particle-accelerator design.
💡 관찰 포인트: 속도 v를 올리면 아래쪽 우주선이 운동 방향(가로)으로: 💡 Observation point: As you increase the speed v, the lower spaceship flattens only along its direction of motion (horizontally). Note that its vertical height does not change at all. At rest (proper length L₀) it is longest, and as v approaches the speed of light c, the length shrinks sharply toward 0.
운동하는 물체의 길이가 운동 방향으로 줄어 보이는 현상(길이 수축)을 이: Understand the phenomenon in which a moving object's length appears shortened along its direction of motion (length contraction).
로런츠 인자 γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²) 와 수축식 L = L₀/γ: Learn the Lorentz factor γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²) and the contraction formula L = L₀/γ.
Distinguish that the length perpendicular to the direction of motion does not change.
Confirm that the length converges to 0 as v approaches the speed of light c.
특수상대성이론에 따르면, 관측자에 대해 빠르게 움직이는 물체는 운동 방향: According to special relativity, an object moving fast relative to an observer is measured as shortened along its direction of motion. The longest length, measured when the object is at rest, is called the proper length (L₀).
줄어드는 정도는 로런츠 인자 γ로 결정된다. v가 작을 때는 γ ≈ 1이: The degree of shortening is determined by the Lorentz factor γ. When v is small, γ ≈ 1 so there is almost no contraction, but as v approaches the speed of light c, γ grows infinitely and the length L = L₀/γ converges to 0. However, the length perpendicular to the direction of motion (height and width) does not change at all.
가로(운동 방향)만 줄고 세로 높이는 같다. 정지 길이 L₀가 항상 가장: Only the horizontal (direction of motion) shrinks while the vertical height stays the same. The rest length L₀ is always the longest.
Common misconception: It is easy to misunderstand that "the object is actually compressed and breaks." Length contraction is not physical compression but a property of spacetime — that lengths measured in different reference frames differ. Also, not all directions shrink; only the direction of motion contracts, while the perpendicular direction is unchanged.
광속의 87%(v ≈ 0.87c, γ ≈ 2)로 달리는 막대의 길이는 정: How is the length of a rod moving at 87% of the speed of light (v ≈ 0.87c, γ ≈ 2) measured compared to its rest length?
정지 길이의 약 2배로 늘어난다: It stretches to about twice the rest length
정지 길이의 약 절반으로 줄어든다: It shrinks to about half the rest length
운동 방향에 수직인 막대의 너비(높이)는 운동할 때 어떻게 될까?: What happens to the width (height) of the rod perpendicular to the direction of motion when it moves?
운동 방향과 똑같이 줄어든다: It shrinks the same as the direction of motion
독일 출신의 이론물리학자. 1905년 \"기적의 해(Annus Mirab: A German-born theoretical physicist. In 1905, his "miracle year (Annus Mirabilis)," he published four revolutionary papers, including special relativity. From the principle of the constancy of the speed of light — that light travels at the same speed in all inertial frames — and the principle of relativity, he derived time dilation and length contraction, overturning the Newtonian worldview of absolute time and space.
길이 수축의 수학적 형태는 헨드릭 로런츠와 조지 피츠제럴드가 에테르 가설: The mathematical form of length contraction was first proposed by Hendrik Lorentz and George FitzGerald within the aether hypothesis, but Einstein reinterpreted it, without any aether, as a property of spacetime itself, completely changing its physical meaning.
1887년 — 마이컬슨·몰리 실험, 에테르 바람을 검출하지 못함: 1887 — Michelson–Morley experiment failed to detect the aether wind
1889~1892년 — 피츠제럴드·로런츠, 운동 방향 길이 수축 가설 제: 1889–1892 — FitzGerald and Lorentz proposed the hypothesis of length contraction along the direction of motion (Lorentz contraction)
1905년 — 아인슈타인, 「운동하는 물체의 전기역학에 대하여」로 특수상: 1905 — Einstein published special relativity in "On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies"
1908년 — 민코프스키, 시간과 공간을 통합한 4차원 시공간 정식화: 1908 — Minkowski formulated four-dimensional spacetime, unifying time and space
과학사적 의의: 길이 수축은 시간 팽창과 함께 절대적 공간이라는 개념을: Historical significance: Length contraction, together with time dilation, abolished the concept of absolute space. The fact that measured values depend on the observer's state of motion shows that spacetime is not a fixed stage independent of the observer. Today relativistic effects are actually measured and used — in particles accelerated close to the speed of light in accelerators, and in the time corrections of GPS satellites.
💡 관찰 포인트: 중심 질량 M을 키우면 격자가 더 깊게 움푹 패이고,: 💡 Observation point: Increasing the central mass M makes the grid dip more deeply and bends the test particle's path more strongly. The particle is not pulled by any "force"; it merely moves along the straightest path (geodesic) on curved spacetime. If the initial speed is too slow it falls to the center, if moderate it orbits, and if very fast it merely bends and passes by (scattering).
Understand the core of general relativity: that mass–energy curves spacetime.
중력을 \"힘\"이 아니라 \"휜 시공간을 따라가는 운동(측지선)\"으로: Learn the view of gravity not as a "force" but as "motion following curved spacetime (a geodesic)."
Know the meaning and limits of the rubber-sheet analogy.
Know that the greater the mass, the deeper the curvature, and that the concept of the Schwarzschild radius arises.
뉴턴은 중력을 질량 사이에 작용하는 힘으로 보았다. 아인슈타인의 일반상대: Newton saw gravity as a force acting between masses. Einstein's general relativity (1915) presents a completely different picture. Mass and energy curve the very spacetime around them, and objects move along geodesics — the straightest paths — within that curved spacetime. What we feel as "being pulled by gravity" is actually the natural motion of following the geometry of curved spacetime.
흔히 쓰는 비유: 팽팽한 고무 막 위에 무거운 공을 놓으면 막이 움푹 들: A commonly used analogy: place a heavy ball on a taut rubber sheet and the sheet dips; a small marble passing nearby bends and circles along the dip, or gets drawn in. The sheet's "dip" corresponds to the curvature of spacetime.
격자가 깊게 패인 중심 주위에서 시험입자의 \"가장 곧은 길\"은 휘어: Around the center, where the grid dips deeply, the test particle's "straightest path" appears curved — this is gravity.
흔한 오개념: \"고무 막 비유에서 공이 패인 곳으로 빨려드는 건 결국: Common misconception: It is easy to think, "in the rubber-sheet analogy, isn't the ball drawn into the dip because of 'gravity pulling downward' after all?" The analogy is only an aid. In reality there is no downward pulling force; what is curved is not only space but spacetime, including time, and the object merely follows the most natural path (geodesic) in that geometry. Moreover, gravity is not a "force" but a geometric effect of spacetime.
일반상대성이론에서 행성이 태양 주위를 도는 이유로 가장 올바른 설명은?: In general relativity, what is the most correct explanation of why a planet orbits the Sun?
태양이 행성을 끌어당기는 인력(힘)이 작용해서: Because an attractive force (a force) from the Sun pulls the planet
태양이 휘게 한 시공간의 측지선을 따라가기 때문에: Because it follows a geodesic of the spacetime that the Sun has curved
행성이 태양의 자기장에 붙잡혀서: Because the planet is held by the Sun's magnetic field
중심 질량 M을 더 크게 하면 주변 시공간은?: If the central mass M is made larger, the surrounding spacetime is?
독일 출신의 이론물리학자. 1905년 특수상대성이론으로 시간과 공간의 절: A German-born theoretical physicist. After overturning the absoluteness of time and space with special relativity in 1905, he started from the equivalence principle — that acceleration and gravity are locally indistinguishable — and completed general relativity over ten years. In November 1915 he published the field equations (Einstein field equations) that describe gravity as the curvature of spacetime.
그는 자유낙하하는 사람이 자신의 무게를 느끼지 못한다는 단순한 통찰(\": Starting from the simple insight that a person in free fall does not feel their own weight ("the happiest thought of my life"), he mathematically proved that gravity is spacetime geometry itself. The help of the mathematician Marcel Grossmann and of Riemannian geometry was decisive.
1687년 — 뉴턴 『프린키피아』, 중력을 질량 간 원거리 인력으로 정식: 1687 — Newton's Principia formulated gravity as an action-at-a-distance attraction between masses
1905년 — 아인슈타인, 특수상대성이론 발표(시공간 개념 등장): 1905 — Einstein published special relativity (the concept of spacetime appeared)
1907년 — 등가원리 착상: 가속도와 중력은 국소적으로 구별 불가: 1907 — Conception of the equivalence principle: acceleration and gravity are locally indistinguishable
1915년 — 일반상대성이론(장방정식) 발표, 중력 = 시공간의 곡률: 1915 — General relativity (the field equations) published; gravity = the curvature of spacetime
1916년 — 슈바르츠실트 해, 블랙홀과 사건의 지평선(rₛ) 개념의 씨: 1916 — The Schwarzschild solution, seed of the concepts of the black hole and the event horizon (rₛ)
1919년 — 에딩턴의 일식 관측, 태양 곁을 지나는 별빛 휘어짐 확인: 1919 — Eddington's eclipse observation confirmed the bending of starlight passing near the Sun → verified the theory
2015~2016년 — LIGO, 중력파 직접 검출로 시공간 동역학 입증: 2015–2016 — LIGO proved spacetime dynamics through the direct detection of gravitational waves
과학사적 의의: 일반상대성이론은 200년 넘게 군림하던 뉴턴의 절대 시공: Historical significance: General relativity replaced Newton's picture of absolute spacetime and action-at-a-distance forces that had reigned for over 200 years, redefining gravity as the geometry of spacetime. From the precession of Mercury's perihelion, the gravitational bending of starlight, and time dilation (GPS corrections) to black holes, gravitational waves, and the expansion of the universe, it became the foundation of modern astrophysics and cosmology. A single sentence — "Matter tells spacetime how to curve, and spacetime tells matter how to move" (Wheeler) — sums up its spirit.
광선의 충돌계수 b (태양 중심 접근거리):: Impact parameter b of the light ray (closest approach to the Sun's center):
💡 관찰 포인트: 노란 실선은 휘어 도착한 실제 광선, 흰 점선은 관측자: 💡 Observation point: The solid yellow line is the actual light ray that arrives bent, and the white dashed line is the apparent direction the observer perceives by extending it backward. Note that the star's apparent position (white dot) is pushed outward, away from the Sun, relative to its actual position (blue dot). Reducing the impact parameter b or increasing the solar mass M makes the deflection angle larger (deflection ∝ M / b). Normally the Sun is too bright to see stars beside it, so only during a total solar eclipse, when the Moon covers the Sun, can this effect be measured.
질량이 시공간을 휘게 하여 빛의 경로도 휘어진다는 일반상대성의 핵심을 이: Understand the core of general relativity: that mass curves spacetime, so the path of light also bends.
Learn that the deflection angle is proportional to the mass and inversely proportional to the impact parameter (closest approach).
일반상대성의 예측(1.75″)이 뉴턴 중력 예측(0.87″)의 정확히 2: Know that general relativity's prediction (1.75″) is exactly twice the Newtonian gravity prediction (0.87″).
Explain why this observation is possible only under the special condition of a total solar eclipse.
일반상대성이론에서 태양 같은 큰 질량은 주변 시공간을 휘게 만든다. 빛은: In general relativity, a large mass such as the Sun curves the surrounding spacetime. Light always follows the "straightest path (geodesic)" of spacetime, but since that spacetime itself is curved, the light ray consequently bends toward the mass. Einstein predicted that starlight from a distant star grazing the edge of the Sun bends by about 1.75 arcseconds (1.75″).
관측자는 빛이 휘어 온다는 사실을 모른 채 도착한 빛의 방향을 곧게 뒤로: The observer, unaware that the light arrives bent, extends the direction of the arriving light straight backward. So the star appears pushed outward, away from the Sun, relative to its actual position. Newtonian gravity (calculating light as a particle) also predicts the bending of light, but its value is only half (about 0.87″), so the two theories could be distinguished by measurement.
휜 광선(노랑)을 곧게 연장하면(흰 점선) 별이 태양에서 바깥쪽으로 밀려: Extending the bent ray (yellow) straight (white dashed line) makes the star appear pushed outward, away from the Sun.
흔한 오개념: \"빛은 질량이 없으니 중력의 영향을 받지 않는다\"고 생: Common misconception: It is easy to think "light has no mass, so it is not affected by gravity." But in general relativity gravity is the curvature of spacetime, and even massless light follows curved spacetime, so its path bends. It is also easy to misunderstand that "the star appears pulled toward the Sun," but in reality, because we perceive the bent light by extending it straight, the star appears pushed outward, away from the Sun.
1919년 에딩턴의 일식 관측이 확인한 것은?: What did Eddington's 1919 eclipse observation confirm?
태양에서 새로운 원소가 발견된다: A new element is discovered in the Sun
태양 가장자리에서 일반상대성이 예측한 빛 편향각(약 1.75″)은 뉴턴: Compared with the Newtonian gravity prediction, the light deflection angle at the edge of the Sun predicted by general relativity (about 1.75″) is?
영국의 천체물리학자로 별의 내부 구조와 항성 진화 연구의 선구자다. 제1: A British astrophysicist and pioneer of research on the internal structure of stars and stellar evolution. Right after World War I he actively introduced the theory of the German scientist Einstein to the English-speaking world, and on May 29, 1919, he led an expedition to verify general relativity's prediction of light bending using a total solar eclipse.
에딩턴 팀은 아프리카 서해안 프린시페 섬으로, 또 다른 팀은 브라질 소브: Eddington's team went to the island of Príncipe off the west coast of Africa, and another team went to Sobral in Brazil, where they photographed the stars of the Hyades cluster near the Sun during the eclipse. Comparing these photographs with the stars' usual (night-sky) positions, they measured how much the stars were pushed outward and confirmed that it matched Einstein's 1.75″ prediction.
1915년 — 아인슈타인, 일반상대성이론 완성. 빛 휘어짐 약 1.75″: 1915 — Einstein completed general relativity, predicting light bending of about 1.75″
1916년 — 슈바르츠실트가 태양 주변 시공간 해를 구함: 1916 — Schwarzschild obtained the solution for spacetime around the Sun
1919년 5월 29일 — 에딩턴의 프린시페·소브랄 일식 원정대 관측: May 29, 1919 — Eddington's Príncipe and Sobral eclipse expedition made observations
1919년 11월 6일 — 영국 왕립학회·왕립천문학회 합동 회의에서 결과: November 6, 1919 — The results were announced at a joint meeting of the Royal Society and the Royal Astronomical Society of Britain
1919년 11월 7일 — 더 타임스 \"과학혁명, 뉴턴 우주관 붕괴\": November 7, 1919 — The Times reported "Revolution in science, Newtonian ideas of the universe overthrown" → Einstein gained worldwide fame
과학사적 의의: 추상적인 이론이 별빛이라는 직접 관측으로 검증된 사건으로: Historical significance: An event in which an abstract theory was verified by the direct observation of starlight, it raised general relativity from speculation to empirical science. It impressed on the public that the Newtonian gravity paradigm, which had reigned for over 200 years, could be replaced by a new theory, and it made the nearly unknown Einstein a worldwide celebrity overnight. Afterward, gravitational lensing became a key tool widely used in modern astronomy to search for dark matter and observe distant galaxies.
💡 관찰 포인트: 광원·렌즈·관측자가 완벽히 일직선(오프셋 = 0)일수록: 💡 Observation point: The more perfectly the source, lens, and observer are aligned in a straight line (offset = 0), the closer the image is to a closed Einstein ring. Increasing the offset breaks the ring into two arcs stretched to either side → with more misalignment it changes into two point images. Increasing the lens mass M makes the Einstein radius (θ_E ∝ √M) larger, spreading the ring/images outward. This phenomenon is used to weigh invisible dark matter and to survey the distant universe.
거대 질량이 시공간을 휘어 빛의 경로를 꺾는다는 일반상대성의 결과를 이해: Understand the result of general relativity that a huge mass curves spacetime and bends the path of light.
Explain that the Einstein radius is proportional to the square root of the mass (θ_E ∝ √M).
광원–렌즈–관측자의 정렬 정도에 따라 상이 고리 → 호 → 이중 상으로: Know that, depending on the degree of alignment of source–lens–observer, the image changes from ring → arc → double image.
Grasp how gravitational lensing is used to measure dark matter and survey the distant universe.
일반상대성이론에 따르면 질량은 주변 시공간을 휘게 하고, 빛은 그 휘어진: According to general relativity, mass curves the surrounding spacetime, and light travels along that curved spacetime. So a huge mass (a galaxy or galaxy cluster) bends the light coming from an object behind it like a convex lens, making the background object appear as several images, stretched arcs, or — when perfectly aligned — a closed Einstein ring.
광원이 렌즈 바로 뒤에 정확히 정렬되면(β = 0) 대칭성 때문에 빛이: When the source is exactly aligned directly behind the lens (β = 0), symmetry makes the light bend equally from all directions, forming a ring. The more the alignment is off (β > 0), the more the ring breaks, leaving two bright images on either side of the lens, and the distance between them is set by the degree of alignment and the mass.
흔한 오개념: \"빛은 질량이 없으니 중력의 영향을 받지 않는다\"고 생: Common misconception: It is easy to think "light has no mass, so it is not affected by gravity." But in general relativity, gravity does not pull light directly; it curves spacetime itself, and light follows the straightest possible path (geodesic) in that curved space, consequently bending. Also, "the lens only gathers light to make it brighter" is only part of the story; the key is that, depending on alignment, several images or a ring appear.
1. 광원–렌즈–관측자가 완벽히 일직선으로 정렬될 때 보이는 상은?: 1. When the source, lens, and observer are perfectly aligned in a straight line, the image seen is?
2. 렌즈 질량 M을 4배로 키우면 아인슈타인 반지름 θ_E는 약 몇 배: 2. If the lens mass M is increased fourfold, about how many times does the Einstein radius θ_E become? (θ_E ∝ √M)
독일 태생의 이론물리학자로, 1915년 일반상대성이론을 완성하며 중력을: A German-born theoretical physicist who completed general relativity in 1915, explaining gravity as "the curvature of spacetime." In 1936 he published a short paper in the journal Science, calculating that if one star were exactly aligned behind another, its light could bend and appear as a ring-shaped image. However, since star–star alignment is so rare, he himself added that "there is little chance it will actually be observed" — what he failed to foresee was that galaxies, far larger than stars, would serve as lenses.
1915년 — 아인슈타인, 일반상대성이론 발표 (중력 = 시공간의 곡률): 1915 — Einstein published general relativity (gravity = the curvature of spacetime)
1919년 — 에딩턴의 일식 관측으로 별빛이 태양 옆에서 휘는 것이 확인: 1919 — Eddington's eclipse observation confirmed that starlight bends beside the Sun
1936년 — 아인슈타인, 별에 의한 빛의 휘어짐과 \"고리 상\"을 계: 1936 — Einstein calculated and published the bending of light by a star and the "ring image"
1937년 — 츠비키(Zwicky), 은하(은하단)가 강력한 중력 렌즈가: 1937 — Zwicky pointed out that galaxies (galaxy clusters) could be powerful gravitational lenses
1979년 — 쌍둥이 퀘이사 QSO 0957+561, 최초로 관측된 중력: 1979 — The twin quasar QSO 0957+561, the first observed gravitational-lensing phenomenon
1998년~ — 약한 중력 렌즈 분석으로 암흑물질 지도와 우주 구조 연구: 1998– — Analysis of weak gravitational lensing launched dark-matter mapping and studies of cosmic structure in earnest
과학사적 의의: 중력 렌즈는 일반상대성이론의 직접적 예측이 우주 규모에서: Historical significance: Gravitational lensing is a case in which a direct prediction of general relativity was realized on a cosmic scale. Today astronomers analyze lens-bent images to measure the distribution and amount of invisible dark matter, and magnify distant, faint objects like a natural telescope to observe them. A phenomenon Einstein called "hard to observe" has become a key tool for peering into the universe today.
💡 관찰 포인트: 거리 d를 키우면 그 은하의 후퇴 속도 v와 적색편이: 💡 Observation point: Increasing the distance d makes that galaxy's recession velocity v and redshift z grow together. In the universe on the left of the canvas, every galaxy recedes from the others simultaneously in proportion to distance (the spatial grid stretches), and the spectral lines of the selected galaxy (yellow outline) shift more toward the red the farther it is (redshift). This is not because we are at a special center, but because space itself is stretching.
Understand that distance and recession velocity are proportional by Hubble's law v = H₀·d.
Know that light from a receding galaxy is redshifted (its wavelength lengthens).
Learn the method of gauging velocity by redshift z ≈ v / c.
Grasp that the expansion of the universe is evidence of the Big Bang.
Explain that our galaxy is not the center; rather, space itself expands.
1929년 에드윈 허블은 멀리 있는 은하일수록 더 빠르게 우리에게서 멀어: In 1929 Edwin Hubble observed that the farther away a galaxy is, the faster it recedes from us. The light of a receding object lengthens in wavelength, so its spectral lines shift toward the red (redshift). The size of this redshift reveals the recession velocity.
거리 d와 후퇴 속도 v는 정비례한다: v = H₀·d. 비례상수 H₀가: Distance d and recession velocity v are directly proportional: v = H₀·d. The proportionality constant H₀ is the Hubble constant, whose current measured value is about 70 km/s/Mpc. This means that a galaxy 1 Mpc (about 3.26 million light-years) away recedes at about 70 km per second. When the velocity is small compared with the speed of light c, the redshift is approximated as z ≈ v / c.
중요한 점은 은하들이 빈 공간을 가로질러 날아가는 것이 아니라, 은하 사: The important point is that the galaxies are not flying across empty space; rather, the space between galaxies itself is stretching. So from whichever galaxy one looks, the farther a galaxy is, the faster it appears to recede.
흔한 오개념: \"은하들이 멀어지니까 우리 은하가 폭발의 중심이다\"라고: Common misconception: It is easy to think "since the galaxies are receding, our galaxy is the center of the explosion." In reality there is no particular center. Because space itself is stretching, from whichever galaxy one observes, the farther a galaxy is, the faster it appears to recede in the same way. Also, the redshift is not because a galaxy flies through space faster than light, but because space stretched while the light traveled, lengthening its wavelength.

미국의 천문학자로, 윌슨산 천문대의 100인치 후커 망원경을 사용해 우주: An American astronomer who completely changed our understanding of the universe using the 100-inch Hooker telescope at Mount Wilson Observatory. In 1929 he compared the distances and recession velocities of several galaxies and announced Hubble's law, that the two are proportional. His name is also given to the Hubble Space Telescope (HST).

1924년 — 허블이 안드로메다가 외부 은하임을 확인(우주의 크기 확장): 1924 — Hubble confirmed that Andromeda is an external galaxy (expanding the size of the universe)

Einstein is said to have regretted the cosmological constant he had introduced to insist on a static universe, calling it "the biggest blunder of my life." The Hubble constant H₀ — the expansion rate of the universe and a key value for gauging its age — is the starting point of modern cosmology, and its precise measurement continues to this day.
💡 관찰 포인트: 왼쪽 하늘 지도는 어느 방향을 봐도 거의 똑같은 온도이: 💡 Observation point: The sky map on the left has almost the same temperature in whatever direction you look (nearly perfectly uniform), and on close inspection there are faint blotches at the level of one part in a hundred thousand (anisotropy) — these are the seeds of galaxies. Raising the temperature T (the hotter universe of the past) shifts the blackbody peak on the right to shorter wavelengths, and at present (2.725 K) the peak comes in the microwave region of about 1 mm. Penzias and Wilson at first mistook this 'noise' that would not vanish from their antenna as due to pigeon droppings, but it was in fact the afterglow of the Big Bang and the closest thing to a perfect blackbody radiation known in nature.
우주배경복사(CMB)가 빅뱅 약 38만 년 후 재결합 시점에 빠져나온 빛: Understand that the cosmic microwave background (CMB) is light that escaped at the time of recombination, about 380,000 years after the Big Bang.
우주 팽창으로 빛이 식어(적색편이) 현재 약 2.725 K의 흑체복사가: Explain that cosmic expansion cooled the light (redshift) so that it is now blackbody radiation at about 2.725 K.
CMB 봉우리가 마이크로파 영역(약 1 mm)에 있고, 빈의 변위 법칙으: Know that the CMB peak lies in the microwave region (about 1 mm) and is set by Wien's displacement law.
거의 완벽히 균일하되 10⁻⁵ 수준의 미세 비등방성이 은하의 씨앗임을 파: Grasp that, while it is almost perfectly uniform, faint anisotropies at the 10⁻⁵ level are the seeds of galaxies.
빅뱅 직후 우주는 뜨겁고 빽빽한 플라스마여서 빛이 전자에 끊임없이 부딪혀: Just after the Big Bang the universe was a hot, dense plasma, so light constantly collided with electrons and could not travel far. About 380,000 years after its birth (recombination), the universe cooled enough for electrons and protons to combine into neutral hydrogen, and light could finally travel freely in straight lines — the universe became 'transparent.' The light that escaped then still arrives from all directions across the sky today.
그 빛은 우주가 팽창하는 동안 함께 늘어나(파장이 길어지는 우주론적 적색: That light cooled as it stretched together with the expanding universe (cosmological redshift, in which the wavelength lengthens). The light, which was visible light of about 3000 K at recombination, cooled while the universe grew about 1100-fold, becoming blackbody radiation at about 2.725 K today, so its peak lies in the microwave (about 1 mm). The CMB is the closest thing to a perfect blackbody known in nature, and the temperature difference by direction is only about one part in a hundred thousand (10⁻⁵). These faint blotches grew under gravity into galaxies and galaxy clusters.
흔한 오개념: \"우주배경복사는 별이나 은하에서 나온 빛이 모인 것\"이: Common misconception: It is easy to think "the cosmic microwave background is light gathered from stars or galaxies." In reality it is light that escaped simultaneously across the whole universe at recombination, long before stars formed. It is also a common misunderstanding that "the CMB comes from one direction of the universe (where the Big Bang happened)," but the Big Bang happened not at a specific point but throughout all of space, so the CMB comes uniformly from every direction of the sky.

Just then Robert Dicke's team at Princeton was searching for the afterglow of the Big Bang, and when the two teams connected, that 'noise' turned out to be the cosmic microwave background. 과학사적 의의: 우주배경복사의 발견은 정상우주론 대신 빅뱅 우주론을 결정: Historical significance: The discovery of the cosmic microwave background was observational evidence that decisively supported Big Bang cosmology over steady-state cosmology. As the predicted afterglow was actually observed — and as a nearly perfect blackbody across the entire sky — it was established that the universe had a beginning. Afterward, the map of faint temperature blotches (anisotropy) became a 'cosmic fossil' that precisely reveals the age of the universe and the proportions of matter, dark matter, and dark energy, forming the foundation of modern precision cosmology.
💡 관찰 포인트: 펌프율이 낮을 때는 원자들이 제멋대로(여러 방향·위상): 💡 Observation point: When the pump rate is low, the atoms undergo only spontaneous emission at random (in various directions and phases). As you raise the pump rate until there are more excited atoms than in the ground state (population inversion), a chain of stimulated emission occurs in which one photon stimulates another excited atom to copy the same photon. The moment the threshold is exceeded, the photons bouncing between the mirrors explode in number, and a coherent, monochromatic beam bursts out of one mirror. Lowering the output-mirror reflectivity increases the loss, so the oscillation threshold becomes higher.
자발 방출과 유도 방출(stimulated emission)의 차이를 구: Distinguish the difference between spontaneous emission and stimulated emission.
레이저 발진의 필수 조건인 반전 분포(population inversio: Understand population inversion, the essential condition for laser oscillation.
펌핑·이득 매질·공진기(두 거울)의 역할과 문턱(threshold) 개념: Learn the roles of pumping, the gain medium, and the resonator (two mirrors), and the concept of the threshold.
유도 방출이 만드는 빛의 결맞음(coherence)·단색성·지향성을 설명: Explain the coherence, monochromaticity, and directionality of the light produced by stimulated emission.
LASER는 Light Amplification by Stimulated: LASER is the acronym for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation. When a photon of the appropriate energy passes an atom in an excited state, that atom emits one more photon with the same wavelength, phase, and direction of travel as the incident photon. This stimulated emission, in which one photon becomes two, is the key to light amplification.
유도 방출이 흡수를 이기려면 들뜬 원자 수(N₂)가 바닥 상태 원자 수(: For stimulated emission to overcome absorption, the number of excited atoms (N₂) must exceed the number of ground-state atoms (N₁). This abnormal state is population inversion, created by pumping — pouring in energy from outside. Placing the gain medium between two mirrors (a resonator) lets photons bounce back and forth and amplify, and when the gain exceeds the threshold set by mirror and transmission losses, oscillation begins. One mirror is made partially transmitting to extract a coherent, monochromatic beam through that gap.
왼쪽 거울은 완전 반사, 오른쪽은 부분 투과. 광자 하나가 들뜬 원자를: The left mirror is fully reflecting, the right partially transmitting. One photon stimulates an excited atom to copy the same photon, amplifying in a chain.
흔한 오개념: \"레이저는 그냥 매우 밝은(센) 빛이다\"라고 생각하기: Common misconception: It is easy to think "a laser is just very bright (intense) light." The key is not brightness but coherence. Ordinary bulb light is spontaneous emission, so its direction, phase, and wavelength are all random, but laser light is copied by stimulated emission so that all photons have the same phase, direction, and wavelength. Also, pumping alone does not unconditionally make a laser; it oscillates only when a population inversion forms and the gain exceeds the threshold where it surpasses the losses.

매질의 온도가 절대 0도일 것: That the medium's temperature be absolute zero
두 거울이 모두 완전 반사일 것: That both mirrors be fully reflecting

단순히 더 밝다(센 빛): It is simply brighter (more intense light)
위상·방향·파장이 일치하는 결맞는 빛이다: It is coherent light with matching phase, direction, and wavelength

1917년 — 아인슈타인, 유도 방출(stimulated emission: 1917 — Einstein theoretically predicted the concept of stimulated emission

과학사적 의의: 레이저는 양자역학(유도 방출)이라는 추상적 이론이 일상: Historical significance: The laser is a representative case in which the abstract theory of quantum mechanics (stimulated emission) was realized as everyday technology. At first its use was so unclear that it was called "a solution looking for a problem," but today it underpins modern civilization — from optical communications (internet optical fiber), barcodes, CDs/DVDs, LASIK surgery, and precision cutting to distance measurement (LIDAR) and gravitational-wave detection (LIGO). It was a turning point that let humanity handle a new form of light: coherent light.
💡 관찰 포인트: 온도 T를 임계온도 Tc 아래로 내려 보세요. Tc를: 💡 Observation point: Try lowering the temperature T below the critical temperature Tc. The moment you cross Tc, the resistance in the upper graph plunges to 0 like a cliff, and the magnet below floats up above the superconductor (Meissner effect). When the resistance is 0, a current that once flows keeps flowing forever. Changing the material preset changes Tc, so the branch point shifts too. Tc is the key branch point that divides everything.
Understand that below the critical temperature Tc the electrical resistance becomes exactly 0.
Know that a resistance of 0 means the current flows forever without decay.
Explain how, through the Meissner effect, a superconductor repels the magnetic field so a magnet floats.
Distinguish that when T > Tc it is an ordinary conductor (finite resistance).
Compare how Tc differs by material and why high-temperature superconductors matter.
대부분의 금속은 온도가 낮아질수록 저항이 서서히 줄지만 0이 되지는 않는: Most metals see their resistance gradually decrease as the temperature drops, but it never reaches 0. However, some materials, when cooled below their characteristic critical temperature Tc, suddenly have exactly 0 resistance. This state is called the superconducting state. Because the resistance is 0, no energy at all is dissipated as heat, so a current that once starts flowing (a persistent current) flows practically forever even without an external power source.
또한 초전도체는 내부의 자기장을 완전히 밀어내는 마이스너 효과(Meiss: In addition, a superconductor exhibits the Meissner effect, in which it completely expels the magnetic field from its interior. As a result, placing a small magnet on top of a superconductor makes it float in the air by the repulsive force (magnetic levitation). If T is higher than Tc, all of these properties vanish and it returns to being an ordinary (normal) conductor.
Tc 위에서는 저항이 유한하지만, Tc를 지나는 순간 저항이 절벽처럼 0: Above Tc the resistance is finite, but the moment it crosses Tc the resistance drops to 0 like a cliff.
흔한 오개념: \"초전도는 그냥 저항이 아주 작은 것\"이라고 생각하기: Common misconception: it is easy to think "superconductivity is just very small resistance." But a superconductor's resistance is not very small—it is exactly 0 (completely gone, below any measurable limit). It is also a misconception that "any material becomes superconducting as long as it is cold enough." Each material has its own characteristic Tc, and only below it does it become superconducting.
임계 온도(Tc) 이하로 냉각된 초전도체의 전기 저항은?: What is the electrical resistance of a superconductor cooled below the critical temperature (Tc)?
평소보다 약간 작아진다: It becomes slightly smaller than usual
초전도체 위에 올린 자석이 공중에 떠오르는 현상의 직접적인 원인은?: What is the direct cause of the phenomenon in which a magnet placed on a superconductor floats in the air?
저항이 0이라 전류가 영원히 흐르기 때문: Because the resistance is 0 so the current flows forever
마이스너 효과로 자기장을 밀어내기 때문: Because it repels the magnetic field via the Meissner effect

느린 중성자 하나가 우라늄-235 핵에 흡수되면 불안정해진 핵이 두 개의: When one slow neutron is absorbed by a uranium-235 nucleus, the destabilized nucleus splits into two lighter nuclei (fragments). This is nuclear fission. 새로 나온 중성자들이 다시 이웃한 핵을 쪼개면 분열이 꼬리를 물고 이어지: When the newly emitted neutrons split neighboring nuclei again, a chain reaction occurs in which fissions follow one after another. The multiplication factor k represents how many subsequent fissions, on average, one fission triggers.
k < 1 (subcritical): fissions decrease each generation and soon die out.
k = 1 (임계): 분열 수가 일정하게 유지된다 → 원자로의 정상 운전: k = 1 (critical): the number of fissions stays constant → normal operation of a reactor.
k > 1 (초임계): 세대마다 분열이 배가되어 기하급수적으로 폭증한다: k > 1 (supercritical): fissions double each generation and explode exponentially → bomb.
중성자가 핵을 맞히기 전에 밖으로 새어 나가면 k가 떨어진다. 그래서 핵: If neutrons leak out before hitting a nucleus, k drops. That is why a fissile material must be gathered above a certain amount (critical mass) for the chain reaction to be sustained. Conversely, inserting control rods that absorb neutrons well lowers k, allowing the reaction to be stopped or slowed.
k≈2인 초임계 연쇄: 세대마다 분열 수가 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 …: Supercritical chain with k≈2: the number of fissions doubles each generation, 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 …
흔한 오개념: \"핵분열 물질을 모으기만 하면 무조건 폭발한다\"고 생각: Common misconception: it is easy to think "a fissile material will inevitably explode just by being gathered." In reality, if the amount is below the critical mass, most neutrons leak out, making k<1 so the chain reaction cannot be sustained. Also, unlike a bomb, a reactor uses control rods to keep k precisely at 1, producing only a steady output, and its structure and enrichment differ so it does not cause a nuclear explosion.
증배계수 k > 1 이면 연쇄반응은 어떻게 되는가?: If the multiplication factor k > 1, what happens to the chain reaction?
원자로가 일정한 출력으로 안정적으로 운전되도록 유지하는 증배계수 값은?: What multiplication factor value keeps a reactor running stably at a constant output?
k = 3 이상으로 키운다: Raise it to k = 3 or more

LIGO가 ~10⁻²¹ 수준의 미세한 길이 변화를 어떻게 검출하는지 안다: Know how LIGO detects minute length changes on the order of ~10⁻²¹.
일반상대성이론에서 질량은 시공간을 휜다. 질량이 가속하면 그 휘어짐의 변: In general relativity, mass curves spacetime. When mass accelerates, the change in that curvature spreads out at the speed of light—this is a gravitational wave. When two black holes orbit each other in a spiral (inspiral), they lose energy to gravitational waves, so their orbit gradually shrinks and their revolution speeds up.
가까워질수록 궤도 진동수가 올라가고 진폭도 커져서, 신호의 주파수와 세기: As they get closer, the orbital frequency rises and the amplitude grows too, producing a chirp waveform in which the signal's frequency and strength surge simultaneously. At the moment of merger the amplitude reaches its maximum, and it dies down into a ringdown stage where the merged black hole stops vibrating. The detected quantity is the strain h = ΔL/L, a minute fractional change in distance, which at LIGO is about 10⁻²¹—a change smaller than a proton.
진동수와 진폭이 함께 커지는 처프(파랑) → 병합 → 빠르게 잦아드는 r: Chirp with frequency and amplitude growing together (blue) → merger → rapidly fading ringdown (red)
흔한 오개념: \"중력파는 일반적인 음파나 전자기파처럼 매질을 통해 전달: Common misconception: it is easy to misunderstand that "gravitational waves are transmitted through a medium like ordinary sound waves or electromagnetic waves." A gravitational wave is not the vibration of a medium but a deformation in which spacetime itself stretches and shrinks, and it propagates at the speed of light even in a vacuum. Also, gravitational waves are so weak that although they are always passing through everywhere in the universe, they were only directly detected for the first time in 2015.

LIGO(Laser Interferometer Gravitational-: LIGO (Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory) is an observatory with L-shaped laser interferometers, each 4 km long, located in Hanford, Washington and Livingston, Louisiana in the United States. Kip Thorne, Rainer Weiss, and Barry Barish led its design and realization, and the three received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2017.

From this change it reads out a length difference of ~10⁻¹⁹ m, smaller than the size of a proton.

과학사적 의의: 아인슈타인이 예측한 지 약 100년 만에 중력파를 직접: Historical significance: By directly detecting gravitational waves about 100 years after Einstein predicted them, humanity opened a completely new observational window to "hear" the universe through the trembling of spacetime rather than through light. Gravitational-wave astronomy has today become a key tool for exploring the universe's most violent events.
💡 관찰 포인트: 가운데 새까만 원이 빛조차 빠져나오지 못하는 사건의 지: 💡 Observation point: The pitch-black circle in the center is the event horizon (shadow), from which not even light can escape. The thin bright band wrapping around it is the photon ring, and the disk rotating on the outside is the accretion disk. The side of the accretion disk approaching us appears brighter (relativistic Doppler asymmetry). Increasing the mass M makes the shadow and the photon ring grow together (rs ∝ M).

Distinguish what the event horizon, photon ring, and accretion disk are.
블랙홀의 '그림자'가 어떻게 보이며 왜 한쪽이 더 밝은지(도플러 비대칭): Explain how a black hole's 'shadow' appears and why one side is brighter (Doppler asymmetry).
EHT가 전 지구 전파망원경을 묶어(VLBI) 지구 크기의 가상 망원경을: Know the principle by which the EHT links radio telescopes across the globe (VLBI) to create a virtual telescope the size of the Earth.
질량 M인 블랙홀에서 빛조차 탈출할 수 없는 경계의 반지름을 슈바르츠실트: The radius of the boundary from which not even light can escape from a black hole of mass M is called the Schwarzschild radius, given by rs = 2GM/c². If the mass doubles, this boundary also grows exactly twofold.
블랙홀 주위에서는 강한 중력이 빛의 경로를 휘게 한다. 그 결과 사건의: Around a black hole, strong gravity bends the path of light. As a result, a dark shadow larger than the event horizon forms, and around it appears a bright photon ring created by light winding around several times. The hot accretion disk formed by infalling gas appears brighter on the side approaching us due to the relativistic Doppler effect. The shadow diameter is roughly about 2.6 times the Schwarzschild radius.
이 그림자는 너무 작아(M87*는 달 위의 도넛 하나 정도의 각크기) 한: This shadow is so small (M87* has an angular size roughly like a single doughnut on the Moon) that it cannot be seen with a single telescope. The EHT is a very-long-baseline interferometer (VLBI) that observes with radio telescopes around the world simultaneously and combines their signals, effectively realizing a virtual telescope with an aperture the size of the Earth, and it first imaged the M87* shadow in 2019.
흔한 오개념: \"블랙홀 사진은 블랙홀 표면을 찍은 것\"이라거나 \"블: Common misconception: it is easy to misunderstand that "a black hole photo captures the black hole's surface" or that "a black hole is a cosmic vacuum cleaner that sucks in everything around it." In reality, what we saw is not the black hole itself but a shadow cast against the background of the gas glowing around it, and a distant object only feels the same gravity as a star of the same mass—it is not sucked in without limit.

EHT는 전 세계 13개 기관, 200명이 넘는 연구자들이 참여한 국제: The EHT is an international collaboration involving 13 institutions and more than 200 researchers worldwide. Radio telescopes located all over the Earth—ALMA in Chile, the JCMT and SMA in Hawaii, and others in Spain, Mexico, and Antarctica (the SPT)—were precisely synchronized with atomic clocks and observed simultaneously. Multiple teams, including one led by Katie Bouman who spearheaded the development of image-reconstruction algorithms, independently reconstructed the images and cross-verified the results. The existence of the black hole shadow became direct visual evidence of the horizon that Schwarzschild predicted in 1916 by solving Einstein's equations, and of general relativity.
