💡 관찰 포인트: 가로축은 붕괴 산물의 불변질량(GeV), 세로축은 사건: 💡 Observation point: The horizontal axis is the invariant mass of the decay products (GeV), and the vertical axis is the number of events. The background is a smoothly decreasing curve, but a small peak rises around 125 GeV. As you increase the statistics (integrated luminosity), the rarely produced signal accumulates and the peak stands out clearly above the statistical fluctuations of the background (significance ∝ √statistics). If you lower the coupling strength to 0, the peak disappears and only the background remains.
힉스 장이 공간을 채우고 있으며, 입자가 이 장과 상호작용하는 정도에 따: Understand that the Higgs field fills space, and a particle gains mass according to how strongly it interacts with this field.
힉스 보손이 힉스 장의 들뜸(입자)이며 질량이 약 125 GeV/c²임을: Know that the Higgs boson is the excitation (particle) of the Higgs field and has a mass of about 125 GeV/c².
드문 신호를 배경 위에서 드러내려면 충돌을 많이 모아야 함(통계의 역할): Explain that revealing a rare signal above the background requires collecting many collisions (the role of statistics).
불변질량 분포의 봉우리와 통계적 유의성(σ)이 \"발견\"의 근거가 됨을: Understand that the peak in the invariant-mass distribution and the statistical significance (σ) form the basis for a "discovery."
표준모형에서 힉스 장은 우주 전체에 0이 아닌 값으로 깔려 있다. 기본: In the Standard Model, the Higgs field is laid out with a nonzero value throughout the entire universe. Elementary particles experience "resistance" to their motion as they interact with this field, and what appears as a result is precisely mass. The stronger the interaction (coupling), the heavier the particle becomes (for example, the photon has zero coupling, so it has no mass).
힉스 보손은 이 힉스 장의 들뜸, 즉 장 자체에 대응하는 입자다. 질량은: The Higgs boson is the excitation of this Higgs field—that is, the particle corresponding to the field itself. Its mass is about 125 GeV/c². When protons are collided at the LHC, a Higgs boson is very rarely produced and immediately decays into other particles (for example, two photons γγ, or four leptons ZZ→4ℓ).
붕괴 산물의 에너지·운동량으로부터 불변질량을 계산해 히스토그램을 그리면,: When you compute the invariant mass from the energy and momentum of the decay products and draw a histogram, most of it is background coming from other processes (smoothly decreasing), but events coming from the Higgs cluster around 125 GeV to form a small peak (the signal). The more collisions you collect (higher luminosity), the more this peak breaks through the background fluctuations and stands out statistically.
Common misconception: it is easy to misunderstand that "the Higgs boson is the cause of all mass." In fact, most of the mass of our bodies or of a proton comes from the strong-interaction energy that binds quarks (E=mc²). What the Higgs mechanism directly explains is the mass of the elementary particles themselves (quarks, leptons, W/Z). It is also not the case that "the Higgs particle is the same as the Higgs field." The Higgs field gives mass, and the Higgs boson appears as the particle that is the excitation of that field.

두 물체 사이에 작용하는 중력: The gravity acting between two objects

1964년 피터 힉스(Peter Higgs)와 프랑수아 앙글레르(Fran: In 1964, Peter Higgs, François Englert, Robert Brout, and others independently proposed a mechanism explaining the origin of mass. About half a century later, in 2012, at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), the two experimental collaborations ATLAS and CMS, together with thousands of researchers, discovered a new particle of about 125 GeV. Higgs and Englert won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2013.

과학사적 의의: 힉스 보손의 발견은 50년 가까이 이론으로만 존재하던 표: Historical significance: The discovery of the Higgs boson is the event that filled in the last piece of the Standard Model, which had existed only in theory for nearly 50 years. It experimentally confirmed how elementary particles acquire mass, and it was a symbolic achievement of modern big-science collaboration, in which thousands of scientists from dozens of countries jointly operated a giant accelerator to "discover" a new particle with a statistical confidence of 5σ (a probability of about 1 in 3.5 million of being a coincidence).

고전 비트는 0 또는 1, 단 두 값만 가집니다. 반면 큐비트(qubit: A classical bit has only two values, 0 or 1. A qubit, on the other hand, exists as a superposition of the two basis states |0> and |1>. This state is fully described by two angles, θ (polar angle) and φ (azimuthal angle), and is visualized as a point on a sphere of radius 1 — the Bloch sphere. The north pole is |0>, the south pole is |1>, and the equator is a 50:50 superposition.
큐비트를 측정하면 더 이상 중첩이 아니라 확률 |cos(θ/2)|²로 0: When you measure a qubit, it is no longer a superposition; it comes out as 0 with probability |cos(θ/2)|² and as 1 with probability |sin(θ/2)|², and at that moment the state collapses to the pole corresponding to the measured value. The quantum gates (X, Z, H, etc.) applied before measurement are operations that rotate the vector on the Bloch sphere — X is a bit flip (|0>↔|1>), and H turns |0> into an equal superposition on the equator.
흔한 오개념: \"큐비트는 0이면서 동시에 1이니까, 한 번 측정하면 0: Common misconception: it is easy to misunderstand that "since a qubit is both 0 and 1 at once, a single measurement can read out both 0 and 1." In reality, at the moment of measurement the superposition collapses and you obtain only a single value, 0 or 1. It is also wrong to think "superposition just means we don't know whether it is 0 or 1" — before measurement there truly is no definite value, only probabilities exist. The power of a qubit lies not in the measured value itself, but in holding multiple states at once before measurement and being able to make them interfere during computation.

When you turn on the path detector, "which slit it passed through" becomes known, so the interference fringes disappear and only a single broad blob remains. 간섭무늬가 확률밀도 I(y) ∝ cos²(ky)·exp(−(y/w)²)로: Learn that the interference pattern is described by the probability density I(y) ∝ cos²(ky)·exp(−(y/w)²).
광자를 한 번에 하나씩 이중 슬릿으로 보내면, 각 광자는 스크린의 한 점: When you send photons through a double slit one at a time, each photon lands randomly at a single point on the screen. Yet once enough photons accumulate, the points gather to form bright and dark stripes — an interference pattern. This is because each individual photon behaves like a probability wave passing through both slits at once and interferes with itself.
만약 \"이 광자가 어느 슬릿을 지났는가\"를 알 수 있는 경로 검출기를: If you place a path detector that can tell "which slit this photon passed through," the path information remains in the environment and the two paths can no longer maintain coherence. As a result, the interference fringes disappear and only a single broad blob distribution remains.
양자 지우개는 그 경로 정보를 다시 지워 어느 슬릿을 지났는지 원리적으로: The quantum eraser again erases that path information, making it impossible in principle to know which slit it passed through. Then, even though the photons still arrive one at a time, the interference pattern is restored. What determines the presence or absence of the pattern is not the intensity of the photons but "whether path information exists."
검출기 OFF → 줄무늬(간섭) / ON → 한 덩어리 / 지우개 ON: Detector OFF → stripes (interference) / ON → a single blob / eraser ON → stripes again (restored).
흔한 오개념: \"광자를 한 개씩 보내면 간섭이 일어날 수 없다\"고 오: Common misconception: it is easy to misunderstand that "interference cannot occur if photons are sent one at a time." In reality, each individual photon, as a probability wave, passes through both paths at once and interferes with itself, so even sending them one at a time produces a pattern once they accumulate. It is also common to think "the detector jostles the photon and destroys the pattern," but the key is not the strength of the collision but the very existence of path information. That is why merely erasing that information (without adding any energy) revives the interference.

존 휠러는 미국의 이론물리학자로 \"블랙홀(black hole)\"이라는: John Wheeler was an American theoretical physicist who popularized the term "black hole" and delved deeply into the measurement problem of quantum mechanics. In 1978 he proposed the delayed-choice experiment. It was a provocative thought experiment about the timing of measurement, holding that even if you decide "whether to measure the path" after the photon has already passed the slits, the result appears accordingly.
1982년 마를란 스컬리와 카이 드륄은 경로 정보를 측정한 뒤 다시 지우: In 1982 Marlan Scully and Kai Drühl put forward the idea of the quantum eraser, in which interference is restored if the path information is measured and then erased again. In 1999 an advanced version, the "delayed-choice quantum eraser" experiment, was reported, precisely showing that the presence or absence of the pattern depends not on the intensity of light but on whether path information exists.

과학사적 의의: 단일 광자 이중 슬릿과 양자 지우개는 양자역학의 상보성과: Historical significance: The single-photon double slit and the quantum eraser are the group of experiments that most vividly demonstrate complementarity and the measurement problem in quantum mechanics. Interference (wave nature) and path information (particle nature) are mutually exclusive, and the boundary between them is determined by the abstract condition of "whether information exists." This insight became the conceptual foundation of decoherence theory, quantum information, quantum cryptography, and quantum computing.

But in 1926 Schrödinger's wave equation describes the electron with a wave function ψ. What we can actually know is only the probability density |ψ|² of finding the electron at a particular position.
Drawing this probability density as a picture is precisely the orbital. The brighter (denser) a region, the higher the chance of finding the electron there.

A classical computer, if unlucky, must check every item one by one, so on average it needs N/2 tries and in the worst case N tries. Grover's algorithm uses quantum superposition and interference to find the answer in about √N tries (a quadratic speedup).
먼저 모든 항목에 동일한 진폭 1/√N 을 주어 균등 중첩 상태를 만듭니: First, give every item the same amplitude 1/√N to create an equal superposition state. Then repeat the following two operations.
오라클(Oracle): 정답 항목의 진폭에만 −1을 곱해 부호를 뒤집습니: Oracle: multiplies only the answer item's amplitude by −1, flipping its sign. ("marking" the answer.)
확산(Diffusion, 평균에 대한 반사): 모든 진폭을 그 평균값을: Diffusion (reflection about the mean): flips all amplitudes about their mean value. The sign-flipped answer is far below the mean, so after reflection it rises far above the mean and its amplitude grows large.
이 두 단계를 거칠 때마다 정답의 진폭(과 확률)이 조금씩 커지고 나머지: Each time these two steps are performed, the answer's amplitude (and probability) grows a little while the rest shrink. This is equivalent to rotating the state vector by a fixed angle toward the answer direction.
\"반복을 많이 할수록 더 정확해진다\"는 틀린 생각입니다. 상태 벡터는: "The more iterations, the more accurate" is a wrong idea. The state vector rotates by a fixed angle at each iteration, so at the optimal number it comes closest to the answer direction, and beyond that it overshoots (over-rotation) and the success probability drops again. That is why the timing of when to stop is important.

In the hydrogen atom the level spacing narrows toward the top, but in the harmonic oscillator the spacing between neighboring levels is always exactly ħω, a constant. This equal spacing is precisely why light (a photon) can excite the vibrational mode one step at a time, and it becomes the foundation for viewing a particle as 'one unit of vibration' in quantum field theory.

This is a direct consequence of Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, that a particle cannot be brought to a complete stop and confined to a single point. The harmonic oscillator is one of the few models that can be solved exactly in quantum mechanics, and nearly every vibrational phenomenon in nature — molecular vibrations, phonons in a crystal lattice, and even the quantization of the electromagnetic field (photons) — reduces to this model. It is the basis for the saying "a physicist sees the universe as a collection of oscillators."

So the wavelength can take only discrete values, λ = 2L/n.

BB84는 두 개의 켤레 기저를 사용한다. 직선 기저 +는 비트 0을 수: BB84 uses two conjugate bases. The rectilinear basis + encodes bit 0 as vertical polarization ↑ and bit 1 as horizontal polarization →, while the diagonal basis × encodes bit 0 as ↗ (45°) and bit 1 as ↘ (135°).
For each photon, Alice picks a random bit and a random basis and sends a polarized photon. Bob, too, picks a random basis for each photon and measures. If Bob's basis is the same as Alice's, he obtains Alice's bit exactly. But if the bases differ, the result becomes random at 50:50 (because in mutually conjugate bases, a definite state in one is a complete superposition in the other).

They publicly cross-check a portion of these as a sample to estimate the error rate QBER. If Eve intercepts and measures-and-resends, the probability that Eve's basis differs from Alice's is ½, and the probability Bob is then wrong is ½ → the error probability at basis-matching positions is ½·½ = ¼ = 25%. That is, the QBER spikes from 0 to about 25%, revealing the eavesdropping.
Even the same bit value has a different polarization direction depending on which basis it was encoded in.

Instead, you measure only the parity of two adjacent qubits to find out which qubit was flipped. The parity tells you the error location without touching the logical information (α, β). Instead, using entanglement via CNOT gates, the logical state is spread across three physical qubits: α|0⟩+β|1⟩ → α|000⟩+β|111⟩. This is not copying but distribution of information.

Here, instead of measuring the qubits themselves, you measure only the parity of adjacent pairs (0 if equal, 1 if different). s1 = q0⊕q1, s2 = q1⊕q2. These two bits are the syndrome, and they point exactly to which qubit was flipped. Applying X to that qubit again to revert it (correction) preserves the logical information α, β without damage.
s1 = q0⊕q1 (위 두 줄), s2 = q1⊕q2 (아래 두 줄): s1 = q0⊕q1 (top two rows), s2 = q1⊕q2 (bottom two rows)

흔한 오개념: \"양자 정보도 그냥 세 번 복사해 다수결로 고친다\"고: Common misconception: it is easy to think "quantum information is also just copied three times and fixed by majority vote." But by the no-cloning theorem an arbitrary quantum state cannot be copied. The 3-qubit code distributes information through entanglement, not copying. It is also misunderstood that "measuring the syndrome collapses the quantum state," but if you measure only the parity, α, β are preserved as is. Finally, this code corrects only a single bit flip (X) — it cannot correct a phase flip (Z) or two simultaneous errors (which is why stronger codes such as the 9-qubit Shor code are needed).

도이치–조자 알고리즘의 원리: The principle of the Deutsch–Jozsa algorithm
함수 f : {0,1}ⁿ → {0,1} 이 다음 둘 중 하나임을 보장(약: Suppose you are guaranteed (promised) that a function f : {0,1}ⁿ → {0,1} is one of the following two.
상수(Constant): 모든 입력에 대해 같은 값(전부 0 또는 전부: Constant: outputs the same value (all 0 or all 1) for every input.
균형(Balanced): 입력의 정확히 절반에 0을, 나머지 절반에 1을: Balanced: outputs 0 for exactly half the inputs and 1 for the other half.
목표는 f가 상수인지 균형인지 판별하는 것입니다. 고전 컴퓨터는 최악의: The goal is to determine whether f is constant or balanced. In the worst case a classical computer must check 2ⁿ⁻¹ + 1 times—one more than half of the 2ⁿ inputs—to be certain. (For n=2, that's 3 times.) But the quantum algorithm gives the answer by calling the oracle just once.
핵심은 보조 큐비트(ancilla)를 |−⟩ = (|0⟩ − |1⟩)/√: The key is to prepare the ancilla qubit in the state |−⟩ = (|0⟩ − |1⟩)/√2. Applying the oracle U_f: |x⟩|y⟩ → |x⟩|y⊕f(x)⟩ to |−⟩ swaps |0⟩ and |1⟩ when f(x)=1, flipping the overall sign. That is, U_f|x⟩|−⟩ = (−1)^{f(x)} |x⟩|−⟩, so the function value is "kicked back" into the phase of the input register.
입력에 하다마드(H)를 걸어 만든 균등 중첩에 이 위상을 실은 뒤 다시: If you load this phase onto the equal superposition created by applying Hadamard (H) to the input and then apply H again, then by interference, when it is constant all phases are equal and fully constructively interfere at |00…0⟩, and when it is balanced they exactly cancel at |00…0⟩.
\"양자 컴퓨터가 모든 입력을 동시에 계산해서 하나하나 읽어낸다\"는 것: "A quantum computer computes all inputs at once and reads them out one by one" is a wrong picture. Measuring a superposition state yields only a single value at random, so you cannot read out all 2ⁿ values of f(x). The power of Deutsch–Jozsa lies in extracting, in one shot through interference, not the individual values but the global property of the whole of f (constant/balanced).

It computes exactly the same formula as the DFT on a quantum state made of N = 2ⁿ amplitudes, but it can be performed with only about O(n²) gates on n qubits, making it exponentially faster than the classical FFT (O(N log N)).
입력 진폭 x[j]를 다음과 같이 출력 진폭 y[k]로 변환합니다. (양: It transforms input amplitudes x[j] into output amplitudes y[k] as follows. (Sign convention of the quantum Fourier transform: the sign of the exponent is +.)
단일 기저 상태 |x₀⟩: 출력의 크기가 모두 1/√N로 균등해지고, 위: Single basis state |x₀⟩: the output magnitudes all become uniform at 1/√N, and the phase rotates linearly as e^(2πi·x₀·k/N) (a phase ramp). That is, the magnitudes are all equal and only the phase turns.
주기적 입력: j = s, s+r, s+2r, … 에서만 진폭이 같은 값: Periodic input: an input that has the same amplitude only at j = s, s+r, s+2r, … and 0 elsewhere concentrates (peaks) at positions k ≈ m·(N/r) in the output. This is the principle by which Shor's algorithm finds the period r.
\"QFT를 적용하면 곧바로 주기 r을 눈으로 볼 수 있다\"는 생각은: The idea that "applying the QFT lets you immediately see the period r with your eyes" is only partly correct. The QFT turns the period into peaks, but on a real quantum computer you have to measure the output, and a single measurement yields only one k. So you obtain the peak positions by sampling several times and then recover r with classical post-processing such as continued fractions. It is also commonly misunderstood that if N/r is not an integer, the peaks are not at exact integer positions but smear out near them.

Once you know r, you can classically compute the factors of N via gcd(ar/2 ± 1, N).

This difficulty is precisely the basis for the security of RSA public-key cryptography. Shor's algorithm solves this problem in polynomial time on a quantum computer, threatening RSA.

고전 컴퓨터로 주기 r 을 찾는 것은 인수분해만큼이나 어렵지만, QFT는: Finding the period r on a classical computer is as hard as factoring, but the QFT transforms all superposed x at once and reveals the period as probability peaks. This is the source of the quantum speedup.

Shor's power lies in interference. 동전을 던져 앞면이면 오른쪽, 뒷면이면 왼쪽으로 한 칸씩 움직이는 것이: Tossing a coin and moving one step to the right for heads and one step to the left for tails is the classical random walk. Since probabilities add at each step, the position distribution becomes a bell shape (binomial/Gaussian) with a peak at the center, and after t steps the spread (standard deviation) is proportional to √t.
양자 걷기에서는 \"동전\"이 큐비트가 되어 중첩 상태를 가질 수 있습니: In the quantum walk, the "coin" becomes a qubit and can have a superposition state. The walker advances to the right and left simultaneously, and the amplitudes of the different paths interfere. As a result, the distribution has two horns (peaks) at the edges, and the spread grows much faster (ballistically) in proportion to t.
한 걸음의 구성: 동전 던지기 + 조건부 이동: Composition of one step: coin toss + conditional shift
상태는 위치 레지스터 x와 동전 큐비트(|↑⟩, |↓⟩)로 이루어지며,: The state consists of a position register x and a coin qubit (|↑⟩, |↓⟩), and has a complex amplitude ψ(x, c) for each position and coin value.
동전 던지기(하다마드): 모든 위치에서 동전에 하다마드 게이트를 적용합니: Coin toss (Hadamard): apply the Hadamard gate to the coin at every position. (a↑, a↓) → ((a↑ + a↓)/√2, (a↑ − a↓)/√2). This operation creates superposition and interference.
조건부 이동(shift): |↑⟩ 성분은 x+1로, |↓⟩ 성분은 x−1: Conditional shift (shift): moves the |↑⟩ component's amplitude to x+1 and the |↓⟩ component's to x−1. The walker's position becomes entangled with the coin state and moves along with it.
t걸음 뒤의 확률 분포는 P(x) = |ψ(x, ↑)|² + |ψ(x,: The probability distribution after t steps is P(x) = |ψ(x, ↑)|² + |ψ(x, ↓)|². Setting the initial coin symmetrically to (|↑⟩ + i|↓⟩)/√2 yields a left-right symmetric two-horn distribution.
\"양자 걷기도 결국 무작위라서 중앙에 몰릴 것이다\"라는 생각은 틀렸습: "The quantum walk is ultimately random too, so it will cluster in the center" is a wrong idea. Until measurement, all paths exist as amplitudes and interfere with one another. Near the center the paths interfere destructively, so the probability actually decreases, while at the edges they reinforce, producing two horns. A single measurement merely draws one position from that probability distribution.

이스라엘의 이론물리학자로, 데이비드 봄과 함께 발견한 아하로노프–봄 효과: An Israeli theoretical physicist, famous for the Aharonov–Bohm effect he discovered with David Bohm. In 1993, together with colleagues, he proposed the concept of the quantum walk, showing that replacing a classical stochastic process with amplitudes and interference fundamentally changes the dynamics. This idea later developed into a key tool of quantum information and quantum algorithms.

In the uniform distribution, every bit string has exactly 1/N probability, becoming a single sharp line, but in the quantum distribution the probability values spread out widely following the Porter–Thomas law P(p) ≈ N·e−Np.
랜덤 회로 샘플링과 양자 우월성: Random circuit sampling and quantum supremacy
n개의 큐비트에 무작위로 뽑은 게이트들을 여러 층 쌓아 만든 회로를 돌린: You run a circuit built by stacking several layers of randomly drawn gates on n qubits, then sample the measured bit strings many times. The probability that each bit string b comes out is the squared amplitude of the state vector, |ampb|². This probability distribution itself looks unremarkable, but to imitate it a classical computer must compute the entire process of 2ⁿ complex amplitudes interfering with one another. As soon as n grows even a little (e.g., 53), 2⁵³ ≈ 9×10¹⁵ amplitudes are needed, making it practically impossible.
얼룩덜룩한 분포와 포터-톰슨 법칙: The speckled distribution and the Porter–Thomas law
충분히 깊은 랜덤 회로를 지나면 출력 확률은 균일하지 않습니다. 간섭 때: After passing through a sufficiently deep random circuit, the output probabilities are not uniform. Because of interference, some bit strings are greatly reinforced and others almost cancel out (speckle). As a result, the distribution of the probability values p follows the Porter–Thomas distribution.
Most bit strings have a very small probability.
A small number of bit strings have an unusually large probability (several times greater than 1/N).
The density of the distribution of probability values is of the form P(p) ≈ N·e−Np (an exponential distribution).
반대로 고전적 추측은 모든 비트열을 똑같이 1/N로 두는 균등 분포입니다: By contrast, the classical guess is a uniform distribution that assigns every bit string the same 1/N. Distinguishing this uniformity from the quantum speckle is the heart of the quantum supremacy experiment.
\"양자 우월성 = 양자 컴퓨터가 모든 문제를 빠르게 푼다\"는 틀린 생: "Quantum supremacy = a quantum computer solves every problem quickly" is a wrong idea. Random circuit sampling is an artificial task with almost no practical use; it merely shows that "it is extremely hard to imitate with a classical computer." It is also wrong that "the output is random and therefore meaningless" — the distribution is not uniform but structured (Porter–Thomas) randomness engraved with interference.
깊은 랜덤 회로의 출력 확률 값 p의 분포는 어떤 모양인가요?: What shape is the distribution of the output probability values p of a deep random circuit?
모든 비트열이 정확히 1/N인 균등 분포: A uniform distribution where every bit string is exactly 1/N
대부분 작은 확률, 소수만 큰 확률 — 지수형 포터-톰슨 분포 P(p)≈: Mostly small probabilities, only a few large — an exponential Porter–Thomas distribution P(p)≈N·e⁻ᴺᵖ

2012년 — 존 프레스킬(John Preskill)이 고전 컴퓨터가 도: 2012 — John Preskill proposes the term "quantum supremacy" to denote the moment a quantum device performs a computation that a classical computer cannot possibly imitate.
2016~2018년 — 랜덤 회로 샘플링이 양자 우월성을 보이기 위한 후: 2016–2018 — Random circuit sampling is proposed as a candidate task for demonstrating quantum supremacy, and it is analyzed that its output follows the Porter–Thomas distribution and what the cost of classical simulation is.
2019년 10월 — 구글이 53큐비트 초전도 프로세서 시커모어(Syca: October 2019 — Google obtains samples in about 200 seconds with the 53-qubit superconducting processor Sycamore, claiming it would take the best supercomputer of the time thousands of years (published in Nature).
2020~2021년 — 중국 연구팀이 광자 기반 지우장(Jiuzhang,: 2020–2021 — Chinese research teams announce similar supremacy experiments with the photon-based Jiuzhang (boson sampling) and the superconducting Zuchongzhi. Meanwhile, IBM and others counter that the gap was exaggerated, citing improvements in classical algorithms.
랜덤 회로 샘플링은 실용적 알고리즘이 아니지만, \"제어된 다수의 큐비트: Random circuit sampling is not a practical algorithm, but it became a milestone in that it first experimentally demonstrated that "a classical computer cannot reproduce the interference distribution created by many controlled qubits." This announced the opening of the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era and sparked active verification-and-rebuttal research on exactly where the boundary between classical and quantum lies.
구글 시커모어 팀 & 존 프레스킬 (John Preskill, 1953~: The Google Sycamore team & John Preskill (1953– )
존 프레스킬은 칼텍의 이론물리학자로 2012년 \"양자 우월성\"이라는: John Preskill is a theoretical physicist at Caltech who put forward the concept and term "quantum supremacy" in 2012. The Sycamore team, led by Google's John Martinis, arranged superconducting qubits in a lattice, built circuits by randomly stacking single-qubit gates and entangling gates between adjacent qubits, and then confirmed with millions of samples that the output distribution matches Porter–Thomas theory.
